top_10.title: First time contributing? Start here.
top_10.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

top_10.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
top_10.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

top_10.title: Is skipping de-risk when a rebuy lacks available margin intentional?
top_10.body:
Hi,

Could you clarify the intended priority between rebuy and de-risk when there is insufficient margin for another entry?

We checked X7 **v17.5.169** (`short_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v3`) and X8 **v18.0.137** (`short_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v4`). The same behavior remains in X7 v17.5.171 and X8 v18.0.140 at commit `c726393`.

When the rebuy conditions pass, the following check returns from the entire adjustment function:

```python
if buy_amount > max_stake:
    return None
```

The de-risk check is located later in the same function, so it is never evaluated in that call—even if its loss threshold has already been exceeded.

Source: [X7](https://github.com/iterativv/NostalgiaForInfinity/blob/c7263935a83b97ed7baa6b8ae0c02741ebe4ae2b/NostalgiaForInfinityX7.py#L79268), [X8](https://github.com/iterativv/NostalgiaForInfinity/blob/c7263935a83b97ed7baa6b8ae0c02741ebe4ae2b/NostalgiaForInfinityX8.py#L61535).

A synthetic short-position example:

- Leverage: **3×**.
- First entry: **1,200 USDT notional / 400 USDT margin**.
- One rebuy has already filled.
- Current P&L: approximately **−607 USDT**.
- Rebuy de-risk threshold: **−560 USDT** (`400 × −1.40`).
- All conditions for the next rebuy pass, but available margin is **zero**.

The callback returns `None`. With the same position, P&L and available margin, making one rebuy indicator condition false allows execution to reach de-risk and return a negative adjustment tagged `derisk_level_3`. We reproduced this with isolated callback tests in both strategies.

**Is holding the position intentional while rebuy conditions remain valid, even when the rebuy cannot be funded? Or should an unaffordable rebuy allow the function to continue to the de-risk check?**

Your clarification would help us distinguish the intended trading policy from an unintended control-flow interaction. We have left the strategy unchanged.

top_10.title: Rebuy mode v3/v4: rebuys 3 and 4 can't fire before rebuy de-risk at 3x or in spot. Intended?
top_10.body:
Hi, this is a question rather than a bug report.

X8 at `5bbcf197a` has these settings (X7 `system_v3_*` has the same):

```python
system_v4_rebuy_mode_stakes_futures = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
system_v4_rebuy_mode_thresholds_futures = [-0.08, -0.12, -0.16, -0.20]
system_v4_rebuy_mode_derisk_futures = -1.40
system_v4_rebuy_mode_derisk_spot = -0.48
```

In `long_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v4`, each rebuy is one first-entry slice. It fires when the price is the threshold below the last entry. Rebuy de-risk fires when `profit_stake < slice_amount * derisk / leverage`.

Take the shallowest possible path, where each rebuy fills exactly at its threshold. In units of the first entry's notional:

| rebuy | price vs first entry | loss when price reaches it | can fire before de-risk only if |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.920 | 0.080 | leverage ≤ 17.5 |
| 2 | 0.810 | 0.310 | leverage ≤ 4.5 |
| 3 | 0.680 | 0.741 | leverage ≤ 1.89 |
| 4 | 0.544 | 1.393 | leverage ≤ 1.0 |

So at the default `futures_mode_leverage = 3.0`, and in spot (0.48 < 0.741), rebuys 3 and 4 can never fire. A deeper path only makes the loss larger. De-risk fires about 6% below the price of rebuy 2.

Backtest check: Binance futures, 3x, 2024-01 to 2026-10, volume top-90 pairlist. Of 603 long rebuy-mode trades, 498 had 0 rebuys, 92 had 1, 13 had 2 and none had a third.

History: on 2025-11-14 the thresholds were widened from `[-0.04, -0.06, -0.08, -0.10]` to `[-0.08, -0.12, -0.16, -0.20]` (X7 3d5ce9a5d, 71c28d530). The rebuy stop stayed at 1.40 and later became the de-risk level (c11c7c557).

Is "first entry + 2 rebuys, then de-risk" the intended design? If so, trimming the arrays to two rebuys would make that explicit. If four rebuys are intended, the de-risk level and the thresholds don't fit together at 3x.

I'm not proposing a behaviour change, only asking whether this is intended.

The de-risk check is located later in the same function, so it is never evaluated in that call—even if its loss threshold has already been exceeded.

Source: [X7](https://github.com/iterativv/NostalgiaForInfinity/blob/c7263935a83b97ed7baa6b8ae0c02741ebe4ae2b/NostalgiaForInfinityX7.py#L79268), [X8](https://github.com/iterativv/NostalgiaForInfinity/blob/c7263935a83b97ed7baa6b8ae0c02741ebe4ae2b/NostalgiaForInfinityX8.py#L61535).

A synthetic short-position example:

- Leverage: **3×**.
- First entry: **1,200 USDT notional / 400 USDT margin**.
- One rebuy has already filled.
- Current P&L: approximately **−607 USDT**.
- Rebuy de-risk threshold: **−560 USDT** (`400 × −1.40`).
- All conditions for the next rebuy pass, but available margin is **zero**.

The callback returns `None`. With the same position, P&L and available margin, making one rebuy indicator condition false allows execution to reach de-risk and return a negative adjustment tagged `derisk_level_3`. We reproduced this with isolated callback tests in both strategies.

**Is holding the position intentional while rebuy conditions remain valid, even when the rebuy cannot be funded? Or should an unaffordable rebuy allow the function to continue to the de-risk check?**

Your clarification would help us distinguish the intended trading policy from an unintended control-flow interaction. We have left the strategy unchanged.

issues.title: Rebuy mode v3/v4: rebuys 3 and 4 can't fire before rebuy de-risk at 3x or in spot. Intended?
issues.body:
Hi, this is a question rather than a bug report.

X8 at `5bbcf197a` has these settings (X7 `system_v3_*` has the same):

```python
system_v4_rebuy_mode_stakes_futures = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
system_v4_rebuy_mode_thresholds_futures = [-0.08, -0.12, -0.16, -0.20]
system_v4_rebuy_mode_derisk_futures = -1.40
system_v4_rebuy_mode_derisk_spot = -0.48
```

In `long_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v4`, each rebuy is one first-entry slice. It fires when the price is the threshold below the last entry. Rebuy de-risk fires when `profit_stake < slice_amount * derisk / leverage`.

Take the shallowest possible path, where each rebuy fills exactly at its threshold. In units of the first entry's notional:

| rebuy | price vs first entry | loss when price reaches it | can fire before de-risk only if |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.920 | 0.080 | leverage ≤ 17.5 |
| 2 | 0.810 | 0.310 | leverage ≤ 4.5 |
| 3 | 0.680 | 0.741 | leverage ≤ 1.89 |
| 4 | 0.544 | 1.393 | leverage ≤ 1.0 |

So at the default `futures_mode_leverage = 3.0`, and in spot (0.48 < 0.741), rebuys 3 and 4 can never fire. A deeper path only makes the loss larger. De-risk fires about 6% below the price of rebuy 2.

Backtest check: Binance futures, 3x, 2024-01 to 2026-10, volume top-90 pairlist. Of 603 long rebuy-mode trades, 498 had 0 rebuys, 92 had 1, 13 had 2 and none had a third.

History: on 2025-11-14 the thresholds were widened from `[-0.04, -0.06, -0.08, -0.10]` to `[-0.08, -0.12, -0.16, -0.20]` (X7 3d5ce9a5d, 71c28d530). The rebuy stop stayed at 1.40 and later became the de-risk level (c11c7c557).

Is "first entry + 2 rebuys, then de-risk" the intended design? If so, trimming the arrays to two rebuys would make that explicit. If four rebuys are intended, the de-risk level and the thresholds don't fit together at 3x.

I'm not proposing a behaviour change, only asking whether this is intended.

issues.title: RG CubeXX: gmloader ports fail at SDL init (no haptic) because mod.txt's -c heuristic forces the vendor SDL2
issues.body:
### Bug report code

_No response_

### Device

Anbernic RG CubeXX

### spruce version

4.5.4

### What happened?

Downwell (PortMaster, gmloader-next) hangs on the loading splash and ignores all input except Menu+Start. log.txt ends with:

  gmloader/main.cpp:257: SDL could not initialize! SDL_Error: SDL not built with haptic (force feedback) support

Cause:
In /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/portmaster/mod.txt, this check runs against the launch script:

  grep -qE '\$GPTOKEYB2?[^&|;]*[[:space:]]-c[[:space:]]' "$0"

Downwell.sh contains `$GPTOKEYB "gmloadernext.aarch64" -c "downwell.gptk" &`, so it matches and /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/h700/lib64/sdl2 is prepended to LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The port ships no SDL2 of its own, so gmloader loads that build, which has no haptic support, and gmloader requires it. The -c flag only means "use this config file", so the heuristic matches nearly every gptokeyb port, not just keyboard-driven ones.

Workaround that fixed it:
Added this to Downwell.sh after get_controls:

  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/mnt/SDCARD/App/PyUI/dll-mali:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH#/mnt/SDCARD/spruce/h700/lib64/sdl2:}"

The game launches and input works afterward, so the dll-mali SDL2 also works with gptokeyb for this port.

Suggestion:
Exempt gmloader ports from the vendor-SDL2 branch (for example, skip it when the script launches gmloadernext), or ship a vendor SDL2 built with haptic enabled.

issues.title: Show Texture shows white screen for large models on Windows with Node.js v24
issues.body:
How did you install WebODM (docker, installer, etc.)?

  Windows installer, version 3.2.8

  What's your browser and operating system? (Copy/paste the output of https://www.whatismybrowser.com/)

Chrome 152 on Windows 11

[glbopti.js](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31883499/glbopti.js)

  What is the problem?

  Clicking "Show Texture" on the 3D model view shows a white screen for any task whose GLB output exceeds 150 MB. CPU briefly spikes, the progress bar moves, then
  the model area goes blank. Smaller models display correctly.

  glbopti.js (which optimizes large GLBs before browser delivery) fails to load because of a broken native binary bundled in a transitive dependency. The
  dependency chain is:

  @gltf-transform/functions → ndarray-pixels → ndarray-pixels/node_modules/sharp@0.35.4
      → ndarray-pixels/node_modules/@img/sharp-win32-x64/sharp-win32-x64-0.35.4.node

  That .node binary fails with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED: The specified procedure could not be found under Node.js v24 on Windows. Because it is loaded eagerly at module
  level, require('@gltf-transform/functions') throws before main() runs, causing glbopti.js to exit with an error. task.py catches the failure and falls back to
  serving the raw unoptimized GLB, which is too large for the browser to render — hence the white screen.

  A secondary issue: even after working around the load crash, compressTexture() from @gltf-transform/functions triggers a libvips error on ODM-generated textures:

  GLib-GObject-CRITICAL: value "32" of type 'gint' is invalid or out of range for property 'space' of type 'VipsInterpretation'
  Error: colourspace: parameter space not set

  This is caused by getTextureColorSpace() returning a value that leads libvips 8.15.3 (bundled with sharp 0.33.5) into an invalid colorspace conversion path.

  How can we reproduce this? (What steps trigger the problem? What parameters are you using for processing? Does it work with the default settings? Include
  screenshots. If you are having issues processing a dataset, you must include a copy of your dataset uploaded on Dropbox, Google Drive or https://dronedb.app)

  1. Run WebODM on Windows with Node.js v24
  2. Process any dataset that produces a GLB larger than 150 MB
  3. Click "Show Texture" on the 3D model view → white screen

  Fix: Two changes to app/scripts/glbopti.js resolve both issues:

  1. Delete node_modules/ndarray-pixels/node_modules/ so ndarray-pixels falls back to the top-level compatible sharp 0.33.5 instead of its bundled incompatible
  0.35.4 binary.
  2. Replace the compressTexture() call with direct sharp calls (texture.getImage() → resize → .jpeg() → texture.setImage()), bypassing the broken colorspace
  detection path.

  A corrected glbopti.js is attached. After applying it and deleting app/scripts/node_modules/ndarray-pixels/node_modules/, a 567 MB GLB with three 24576×24576
  textures processes and displays correctly.

issues.title: [Feature]  Explicitly requested tasks
issues.body:
## Problem / motivation

Explicitly requested tasks are currently handled through alert evaluation. A request can receive a “Created” response after being submitted for evaluation, without a persistent task being saved or appearing in “Needs you.”

This makes it difficult to determine whether a task exists, track its progress, or mark it completed. Acknowledging an alert also does not necessarily mean the underlying work is finished.

## Proposed solution

Add persistent user tasks with a lifecycle independent of alert evaluation.

Each task should have:

- A stable ID.
- Title and description.
- Owner.
- Status: open, in progress, waiting, or completed.
- Optional due date.
- Creation, modification, and completion timestamps.
- A reference to the originating conversation or message.

When a user explicitly requests a task, save it immediately and confirm creation only after storage succeeds. Alert evaluation may enrich or escalate the task, but should not determine whether it exists.

Allow users to view, update, complete, and reopen tasks through the UI and chat. Provide authenticated API endpoints for the same operations, with pagination, filtering, ownership checks, and conflict detection.

Completed tasks should be hidden from active views by default but remain accessible in history.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use alerts as tasks:** Alert acknowledgement and dismissal do not accurately represent task progress or completion.
- **Use activity logs:** Logs record submissions but do not provide a reliable task lifecycle.
- **Require tasks to pass alert evaluation:** Explicit user commitments should persist regardless of their urgency or relevance score.

## Scope

- [x] Backend (`packages/core`)
- [x] UI (`packages/ui`)
- [ ] A new specialist agent
- [ ] An integration (Slack / Email / Telegram / Discord / Google Chat)
- [ ] Deployment / infrastructure
- [x] Docs

## Additional context

Tasks and alerts should have distinct purposes:

- **Task:** Work someone has committed to doing.
- **Alert:** Information selected for someone’s attention.

They may be linked, but acknowledging or dismissing an alert should not automatically complete its associated task.

### Acceptance criteria

- Explicitly requested tasks persist independently of alert evaluation.
- Creation is confirmed only after successful storage.
- Users can update status, complete tasks, and reopen them.
- UI, chat, and API reflect the same saved task state.
- Completed tasks are excluded from active views by default.
- Repeated requests or retries do not create unintended duplicates.
- Failed operations report an error without claiming success.

issues.title: Issues with scrollbar use in `Page` template main area
issues.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
In classic templates (Vanilla, Bootstrap, Fast, Material...), the scroll bar allowing to navigate within the main area was all the way to the right of the window which meant the cursor could be anywhere in the main area and it worked, even outside the actual main area container.

With `pn.ui.Page`, the scroll bar is within the main area container itself, with no margin, which proves frustrating to users.

First because on the web, to scroll through the main content of a page, you don't usually have to worry much about the position of your cursor. Plus, here it can become really bad if the main area is filled with elements that themselves can capture scroll events, such as plots, then the actual area where the scroll will reliably work can become vanishingly small. It's essentially only two tiny vertical bands on both sides of the plots.

Second, if you're looking for the scroll bar to actuate it by clicking on it, it's natural to look for it at the edge of the window.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
The idea would be to make `pn.ui.Page` behave like classic templates in that regard.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I think one could set a larger main area width and then place the actual content between two spacers. But still you may not necessarily end up with the scroll bar at the edge of the window.

Attached is an example showing how hard it becomes to scroll within a main area filled with holoviews plots. Unfortunately the cursor is not visible but you get the idea.

```python
import holoviews as hv
import numpy as np
import panel as pn

pn.extension()

plots = pn.ui.Column(
    *[
        hv.Curve(np.random.randn(100)).opts(height=400, responsive="width")
        for _ in range(5)

)

    sidebar_width=250,

)

    main=[plots],
    sidebar_width=250,
    sidebar=["## I'm the sidebar"],

)

page1.servable()
```

Flow scheduler stops firing jobs after some hours (eventlet worker); next_run_time stays in the past
issues.body:
Scheduled flows stop running without any error. The jobs stay in the jobstore, but their `next_run_time` stays in the past and nothing executes. Saving or re-activating a flow logs "Added job flow_workflow_N" with the new trigger time, but the job still doesn't fire. Manual runs keep working the whole time.

**Evidence** (checked on 2026-10-30 at about 09:02 IST)
Reading the jobstore table (`FLOW_JOBSTORE_TABLE`):

```
flow_workflow_23 2026-10-29 11:35:10   # interval flow, stuck since yesterday
flow_workflow_24 2026-10-29 11:36:02
flow_workflow_25 2026-10-29 11:36:02
flow_workflow_1  2026-10-30 08:55:00   # daily trigger, didn't fire at 08:55
```

At 08:54 the logs show `Creating daily trigger: 08:55` and `Added job flow_workflow_1`, but there's no log line at all at 08:55:00.

After `docker restart openalgo-web`, every job got a new future `next_run_time` and started firing again.

**Environment**

- Docker on ARM64 (Ubuntu).
- `gunicorn --worker-class eventlet --workers 1`.
- Container TZ, `tzlocal`, and the scheduler timezone are all `Asia/Kolkata`, so timezone isn't the cause.
- `BackgroundScheduler` with `SQLAlchemyJobStore` and `misfire_grace_time=60` (`services/flow_scheduler_service.py`).

**Suspected cause**
`BackgroundScheduler` runs in a thread under eventlet's monkey patching. The scheduler's wake-up thread seems to stall, so jobs are added but never woken. Possible fixes:

- Use `GeventScheduler` or an eventlet-friendly scheduler.
- Run the scheduler in a separate process.
- Add a watchdog that restarts the scheduler when a job's `next_run_time` falls behind.

Also, `misfire_grace_time=60` means a job that stalled is skipped instead of caught up. A missed scheduled run should at least be logged.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Activate flows with interval and daily schedule triggers.
2. Leave the container running for several hours. In my case it stalled about 1 hour after re-importing the flows on the previous day.
3. Check the jobstore `next_run_time` values. They're in the past and nothing runs until the container restarts.

issues.body:
### Existing issues

- [x] I searched open issues and this is not already requested.

### Problem

An edition can add a remote-provisioner lane: `registerRemoteProvisionerRenderer` draws its launch form. But once a crew is launched, its row in **Your crews** has no lifecycle controls. Stop / Start / Delete in the row menu exist only for EC2 crews, addressed by the launch tag.

So an edition that needs Start / Stop for its own machines must draw a second list of the same crews. Every crew then shows up twice, and only one copy has the buttons.

### Proposed behaviour

A frontend seam, `registerCrewRowActions`, keyed by the row's `provisioner_id` stamp. A contribution supplies up to two components, each handed the row:

- `menuItems`: extra items in the row's overflow menu, between Edit and Remove.
- `detail`: a block under the row header (the machine's state, an action in progress, its error).

Rules: the core registers nothing; `aws_ec2` cannot be claimed; a chained row (whose stamp the announcing pane chose) gets nothing; each component sits in an ErrorBoundary. Actions still go through the edition's own routes, which authorize server-side.

### Alternatives considered

Keep the edition's second list. It duplicates every crew and splits one crew's controls across two places.

Remote Crew (Settings → Remote Crew → Your crews)

issues.title: Agent message persistence commits SQLite synchronously on the controller loop
issues.body:
Part of the #2706 family (SQLite work on the controller loop). Found in the v3.2.1 post-tag upgrade run on a slow disk. Present since at least 3.2.0. Targets 3.2.2.

## Evidence

On the first Turn after the migration, the loop stalled for 3.0 s, 2.8 s and 3.9 s. The loop thread's stack, innermost frames last:

```
modules/agents/vibey/agent.py _settle → base.emit_result_message
core/controller.py emit_agent_message
core/message_dispatcher.py emit_agent_message → persist_agent_message
core/message_mirror.py persist_agent_message: with engine.begin() as conn
sqlalchemy ... do_commit → dbapi_connection.commit()
```

The wait is in the **commit** itself, not in acquiring SQLite's writer. On a slow disk, a commit's `fsync`, plus any WAL auto-checkpoint the commit triggers, runs synchronously on the loop thread. The test install's database was only 840 KB, which points at `fsync` latency rather than a large checkpoint.

## Why it is not a simple move to a thread (the #2708 check)

`persist_agent_message` runs for every persisted output: results, notices, interim rows, and hosted/tool-call trace rows. It runs on the loop today, so persists commit in the order the loop issued them. Two loop sections depend on that order:

1. **Within one emit.** The emit uses the persisted row (`persisted_output`): its id feeds delivery evidence and the Run's terminal record (`message_id`). Awaiting an off-loop persist in place keeps this order.
2. **Across concurrent emits for the same Session.** For example, a receiver's result and a concurrent Activity-output flush. The transaction assigns the row's position and transcript rank (`rank`, `message.new`, inbox). On the runtime-work executor, which has several threads, two persists could commit in the opposite order from the one the loop issued them in, and the transcript order would change.

The ordering requirement rules out the general door as is: transcript order must stay loop order.

## Proposed shape

Persist through an **ordered writer**: a single-thread executor that commits persists in the order the loop submitted them. Each emit awaits its own persist under the `_store_step` rule (#2715), so cancellation points stay where they are on master.

The post-commit publishes (`message.new`, `inbox.session.updated`, activity) go out from the loop after the commit lands, in the same order.

`persist_silent_terminal` and the other `message_mirror` writers go through the same writer.

## Placement

Right after path A (#2715), as A2: same emit path, same cancellation rule. Before B step 2. A short design check on the ordered writer comes first, covering:
- that cross-Session order needs no stronger guarantee than per-submission order;
- how the writer drains at shutdown;
- the plan-test-style regression: a held writer must not hold the loop, and two concurrent emits must keep their order.

clai REPL crashes on unknown slash commands or error text that looks like Rich markup
issues.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the [latest version](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases/latest) of Pydantic AI
- [x] I've searched for my issue in [the issue tracker](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues) before opening this issue

### Description

### What I see

In the interactive `clai` REPL, typing an unrecognized slash command whose text looks like Rich markup (e.g. `/foo[/bar]`) raises an uncaught `rich.errors.MarkupError` and kills the session with a traceback instead of printing “Unknown command” and continuing.

The same pattern affects the REPL error handler: exception text (and `__cause__`) is interpolated into `console.print(...)` markup strings without escaping, so a failure message that contains `[/...]` (HTTP bodies, paths, JSON, etc.) can crash the session while trying to print the handled error.

### What I expect

- Unknown slash commands are shown literally (e.g. `Unknown command `/foo[/bar]``) and the REPL keeps running.
- Run failures print the exception message literally and the REPL keeps running.

### Where it happens

`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_cli/__init__.py`:

- `handle_slash_command` — unknown command / unknown `/usage` option embed `ident_prompt` in Rich markup.
- `run_chat` — calls `handle_slash_command` without `try/except` (unlike the `ask_agent` branch).
- `run_chat` exception handler — embeds `{e}` and cause text in markup strings.

### Severity

High — normal user input at the `clai ➤` prompt, no malicious intent required.

### Interactive repro

1. Start `clai` (or `pydantic-ai` chat).
2. At the prompt, type: `/foo[/bar]`
3. Session exits with `MarkupError`.

### Logfire

Not applicable — local CLI / Rich rendering only; no model request required for the minimal repro below.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

```Python
import io

from rich.console import Console

from pydantic_ai._cli import handle_slash_command

# Uncaught on current main: MarkupError instead of "Unknown command"
handle_slash_command("/foo[/bar]", [], False, Console(file=io), "default")
```

### Logfire Trace

N/A — reproducible without a model call or Logfire.

issues.title: Docstring descriptions for `*args` and `**kwargs` are ignored in tool schema
issues.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the [latest version](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases/latest) of Pydantic AI
- [x] I've searched for my issue in [the issue tracker](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues) before opening this issue

### Description

If a tool function documents `*args` or `**kwargs` in its docstring the usual Google way (`*args: ...`, `**kwargs: ...`), the description is dropped from the tool schema. With require_parameter_descriptions=True, the tool fails to register with "Missing parameter descriptions".

Griffe keeps the stars in the parsed name (`*words`, `**options`), but the schema looks it up as `words`/`options`. NumPy and Sphinx docstrings have the same problem.

Expected: the description of `*words` shows up on the `words` parameter (and likewise for `**kwargs`), and no error.

I have a fix ready in #12126.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

```Python
from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent('test')


@agent.tool_plain(require_parameter_descriptions=True)
def join_words(sep: str, *words: str) -> str:
    """Join words with a separator.

    Args:
        sep: The separator to put between words.
        *words: The words to join.
    """
    return sep.join(words)


print(agent.run_sync('hi').output)
# UserError: Error generating schema for join_words:
#   Missing parameter descriptions for words
```

### Logfire Trace

_No response_

### Python, Pydantic AI & LLM client version

- Python: 3.13
- Pydantic AI: 2.64.0
- LLM provider SDK: none (TestModel)

issues.title: Document how to test agent skills and library changes through MCP in a live Revit
issues.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

Changing agent skills or the pyrevitlib helpers they describe is best verified by running the snippets in a live Revit through the MCP server. Nothing in the repo describes that workflow, so every contributor (human or agent) rediscovers it. `docs/agent-runtime.md` documents the in-Revit "Agent Tests" buttons and `AGENTS.md` documents the build and `pyrevit clones add` / `attach`. The steps in between are missing, and each one failed while I worked on #3839 (PR #3863):

- **A rebuild fails while any `pyrevit mcp` server is running.** Each MCP client session starts `bin\pyrevit.exe mcp`, which holds files in `bin\` (for example `Colorful.Console.dll`). `BuildLabsModule` then fails with "The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process". The server of every open client session holds the lock, not only the current one.
- **Python and markdown changes under `pyrevitlib` need no rebuild.** IronPython can `reload()` them. CPython cannot: reloading `pyrevit.revit.db.create` fails with `TypeError: Duplicate type name within an assembly` because `FamilyLoaderOptionsHandler` is baked once. A restart of Revit is the reliable way to load edited modules on both engines.
- **The "Security - Unsigned Add-In" dialog appears after every rebuild and restart** and has to be accepted ("Load Once") before the MCP host answers. `docs/ci-cd.md` mentions this dialog only as a CI failure.
- **How to test a snippet or helper is undocumented:** run it through `run_query` in a scratch family or project document (`app.NewFamilyDocument`, `app.NewProjectDocument`), close the document in `finally`, and restore any user setting touched (for example `app.SharedParametersFilename`). If a script fails with a transaction open, `Close(False)` raises and hides the real error, so roll back first.

## Describe the solution you'd like

- A short section "Testing agent skills and library changes through MCP" in `docs/agent-runtime.md` that covers the steps above in order:
  - when a rebuild is needed (C# changes) and when a restart or reload is enough (Python and markdown)
  - stopping running `pyrevit mcp` processes before a rebuild, and that clients must reconnect afterwards
  - accepting the unsigned add-in dialog after each start
  - engine differences when reloading modules
  - running a snippet in a scratch document and cleaning up
- A one-line pointer to that section from `AGENTS.md`, which should stay a list of conventions and commands.
- Optionally, a small dev-tools command or script that stops the `pyrevit mcp` processes started from the clone's `bin\` before a build.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Put the whole procedure in `AGENTS.md`. It is loaded for every task and is meant to stay lean, so a pointer is enough.
- Leave it to the contributor. This is what happens now: one failed build and several extra runs before the cause of the lock was clear.
- Keep it in a personal notes file. That helps one person and not other contributors or their agents.

## Additional context

Found on Revit 2024.1, Windows 11, a Debug build of `develop`, IronPython 2.7.12 and CPython 3.12.3. Related: #3839, PR #3863.

issues.title: 413 请求体超限死锁：压缩请求也被挡，面板缺少上限开关
issues.body:
## 错误

图片型会话 token 压力 51%（509,860 / 1,000,000），请求体 16,967,637 bytes > 16,777,216，网关返回：

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "payload too large (16967637 bytes > 16777216 limit)",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": 413,
    "gateway_hint": "single request body exceeds the gateway cap (WB_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, default 16MB); raise it and restart wb-proxy"
  }
}
```

之后每轮都 413；`/compact` 发出的压缩请求也是普通 `/v1/messages` 请求，同样 413，死锁。

## 根因

- 413 在读 body 时就抛出（`_read_payload` 的大小检查 `wb_proxy.py:19689` → `_payload_or_error` `wb_proxy.py:19708`），发生在路由分发和任何压缩识别之前（调用点 `wb_proxy.py:22493`），压缩请求没有临时放宽。
- 413 文案是英文，只说 `raise it and restart wb-proxy`，没告诉用户可以发压缩请求或在面板调上限。
- `WB_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` 是启动环境变量（`wb_proxy.py:42`），面板没有开关。
- 字节 cap 不能改成 token：16MB 图片约 1 万 token，16MB 文本约 440-560 万 token。

## 修复建议

1. **413 改成中文、可行动**：

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "请求体过大（16967637 字节 > 16777216 字节）",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": 413,
    "gateway_hint": "请发送压缩请求（/compact）缩小上下文，或在网页面板「设置 → 单请求体上限」临时调高（当前 16MB）。"
  }
}
```

2. **面板增加「单请求体上限」MB 开关**：默认 16，范围 1-256，保存即生效（或提示重启）。

3. **压缩请求临时放宽到 64MB**：只对能识别的压缩请求生效；判定放在读 body 之前（header 此时已可读），给 `_read_payload` 传 64MB。普通请求仍 16MB。

issues.title: [yaxuanm/qdrant] Hybrid Search fails on named-vector collections (dense/sparse)
issues.body:
## Plugin
yaxuanm/qdrant v0.0.1

## Problem
Hybrid Search fails on collections with named vectors (`dense`, `sparse`) created outside the plugin (e.g. custom embed scripts).
**Error:** Qdrant responded with HTTP 400: Wrong input: Not existing vector name error:


## Root cause
1. Operation inference checks `text` before hybrid indicators → runs `operation: "query"` instead of `hybrid_search`
2. Plain query sends unnamed `vector` to `/points/search` — invalid when collection has only named vectors
3. Sparse vector is not generated from `text` in hybrid path (only dense embedding is created)
## Reproduction
- Collection: named vectors `dense` (3072) + `sparse`
- Tool: Qdrant · Hybrid Search
- Inputs: `text`, `using_dense: dense`, `using_sparse: sparse`, `fusion_method: rrf`
- Embedding: text-embedding-3-large
## Expected
`hybrid_search` → `/points/query` with prefetch using `dense` and `sparse`
## Actual
`query` → `/points/search` with flat `vector` array (no vector name)
## Fix verified locally (v0.0.2)
- Route hybrid before text→query
- Set `operation: hybrid_search` on hybrid tool YAML
- Generate sparse via `fastembed` (`Qdrant/bm25`)
- Add `fastembed` dependency
## Environment
- Dify 1.14.2 (self-hosted)
- Qdrant Cloud
- Plugin: yaxuanm/qdrant 0.0.1 from Marketplace

issues.title: Plugin request: Hive — social media management (OpenAPI 3.1 + remote MCP)
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

Hive

### Function Description

Social media management inside a Dify workflow: publish and schedule across twelve networks, read cross-account analytics, work a shared inbox, and build DM automations for Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and TikTok.

Scenarios people would build:
- An agent drafts a post, validates it against each network's rules, and schedules it
- A scheduled workflow pulls last week's numbers across every connected account and writes a summary
- A form submission becomes an idea on the content board

Everything needed to build the plugin is already published:

- **OpenAPI 3.1**: https://hivepublish.com/api/v1/openapi.json — 50 endpoints, one per tool, each with an operationId, responses and a description
- **Auth**: bearer token — a scoped API key from Hive (Settings → API) or an OAuth 2.1 access token
- **Remote MCP server**: https://hivepublish.com/api/mcp (OAuth 2.1 + dynamic client registration), listed on the official MCP Registry as `com.hivepublish/hive`
- **Docs**: https://hivepublish.com/developers

Good first tools: `create_draft`, `schedule_post`, `read_analytics_summary`, `read_posts`, `read_calendar`, `search`, `fetch`.

One behaviour worth modelling: anything that would reach a real audience — scheduling, public replies, direct messages, setting an automation live — does not execute on the API call. It returns a single-use approval URL that the account holder confirms inside Hive, and the call is re-sent with that token. Reads and draft creation run immediately. A plugin should surface the approval URL as output rather than treat it as an error.

### Official Website URL

https://hivepublish.com — docs at https://hivepublish.com/developers

issues.title: `UniXNU-sheng` cannot build on a clean checkout: `build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json` is required but no repository ships it
issues.body:
`./unixnu build kernel -D ../UniXNU-sheng` stops at archive-10 on a clean checkout because
`scripts/build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py` requires `build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json`, which is
produced only by `scripts/audit-storage-interface.py` — and that script needs staged qualification
evidence (a specific prelinked candidate, two live `gdb-stop.json` snapshots and a KDK reference)
that cannot be produced from a clean tree, and is not in any repository.
`build-software-aes-bindings.py` already falls back to a recorded result for exactly this situation
(`scripts/data/native-aes-original-bindings.S`). Could the storage audit get the same treatment, or
could the audit record itself be published?
## Environment
| | |
| --- | --- |
| UniXNU | `ae687009348296e97e49ce6e925795044f363ce6` |
| UniXNU-sheng | `08cde20edc32` |
| OS profile | `ipados-17.7.11-21H461` (`[kernel.prelink] kernelcache_sha256 = f18b4df865405f2a287b84977d7aca745e056d656d9fc9df1662970ce2969de7`) |
| Host | macOS 26.7.1, Intel i5-9600KF (x86_64, 6 cores), Xcode 26.5, Python 3.15.1 |
| QEMU | `qemu-system-aarch64` (TCG; HVF is Apple-Silicon-only, so TCG is the only option here) |
## Reproduction
```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU
git clone https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng
cd UniXNU
./unixnu defconfig sheng_defconfig -D ../UniXNU-sheng
./unixnu build kernel -D ../UniXNU-sheng
```
## Actual result
`archive-06` (AES) passes with `PASS: native AES bound with the recorded original-kernelcache addresses`.
`archive-10` fails with a raw traceback:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../tree/scripts/build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py", line 20, in <module>
    audit = json.loads((ROOT / 'build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json').read_text())
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
  '.../tree/build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json'
```
The same failure should occur on `macos-26` in the documented workflow, whose default dispatch is
`UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng` + `sheng_defconfig` + `steps=kernel`:
```sh
gh workflow run macos.yml -f device_repository=UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng -f defconfig=sheng_defconfig -f steps=kernel
```
## Why a clean tree cannot produce it
1. `sheng_defconfig` enables `CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK=y` and `CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_RAM_BLOCK=y`,
   and `[kernel] archives` places the two `build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py` entries after
   `component:VirtioMmioBlock` / `component:RamBlock`. The builder reads the audit unconditionally.
2. The kernel step's `storage-headers` pass only prepares headers:
   `scripts/prepare-storage-headers.py` writes `build/storage-abi/headers.json` with
   `qualification: false`, and its own docstring says the audit "additionally needs the live guest
   metadata snapshot and the original kernel candidate".
3. `scripts/audit-storage-interface.py` has no CLI and hardcodes its inputs:
   - `build/xnu-prelink/native-apfs-load-positive.macho` + `.json`
   - `build/darwinboot-storage-native-metadata/gdb-stop.json` (must match `kernel_sha256`, must carry
     `TCR_EL1`/`SCTLR_EL1`/`TTBR0_EL1`/`TTBR1_EL1` and 0x50-byte dumps at both metaclass addresses)
   - `build/image4-ignition/aes-interface-audit.json`
   The candidate is itself the output of a prelink, which runs *after* the archives, so the chain
   cannot bootstrap itself.
4. `/build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:2`), so the artifact exists only in a workspace where the
   qualification was actually performed.
I searched for it rather than assuming: the string `abstract_complete_destructors_trap` (written only
by this audit) appears in the repository only in `scripts/audit-storage-interface.py` and
`scripts/build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py`; it is absent from `UniXNU-sheng`,
`UniXNU-sm8550-common`, `profiles/`, and from every tree fetched by `unixnu fetch`.
`git log -S 'interface-audit.json'` returns only the initial import and one docs commit — no data file
was ever added.
`docs/porting/migration.md` ("sheng build inputs") does list `storage-abi/interface-audit.json` as a
required input, so this looks like an intentional local input — but it is currently a hard blocker
for anyone building `sheng` from source, including CI.
## Precedent for a fix
`scripts/build-software-aes-bindings.py` already does the right thing when the qualification evidence
is absent:
```python
audit_path = ROOT / 'build/image4-ignition/aes-interface-audit.json'
recorded = ROOT / 'scripts/data/native-aes-original-bindings.S'
if not audit_path.is_file() and recorded.is_file():
    # Without the qualification evidence of the original kernelcache (kernel candidate, KDK
    # annotations, live metadata), bind with the recorded result of that audit. The addresses
    # belong to the kernelcache pinned in board.toml.
    ...
    print('PASS: native AES bound with the recorded original-kernelcache addresses')
```
That is why archive-06 passes and archive-10 does not.
## Proposed change
Either is fine; the first is preferred:
1. **Publish the record and add the same fallback.** Commit the audit as a pinned record (for example
   `scripts/data/storage-abi-interface-audit.json`) and let `build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py` read it
   when `build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json` is absent, with the same note: the addresses belong
   to the kernelcache pinned in `board.toml`. Note the builder already accepts a *missing*
   `native-apfs-load-positive.macho` ("the audit JSON is the pinned record"), so only the JSON has to
   be shipped.
2. **Document the staging.** If the record must stay unpublished, add the exact commands that
   produce it (candidate, QEMU fixture invocation, both snapshots, KDK version and kext hash) to the
   porting record and to the macOS workflow's `pre_build` documentation, so a contributor can
   reproduce it rather than guess.
The JSON contains only addresses, hashes, layout constants and booleans — no device identity — so
publishing it does not leak anything comparable to the platform seed.
## Workaround in use meanwhile
Disabling the native VirtIO/RAMBlock path and removing the two builder entries lets the kernel step
proceed:
```diff
-CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK=y
-CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_RAM_BLOCK=y
-CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK_ARCHIVE="{tree}/build/virtio-mmio-block-verified-bundle/libVirtioMmioBlock.a"
+CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK=n
+CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_RAM_BLOCK=n
+CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK_ARCHIVE=""
```
That is acceptable for real-hardware work (`ShengUfs` covers storage) but it removes the QEMU
storage-verification path, which is presumably the opposite of what you want tested in CI.
## Minor, same area
The missing-input case surfaces as a raw `FileNotFoundError` traceback instead of an `unixnu` error
with a hint. For an expected qualification gap, a clear message (like the platform-seed one) would
help — e.g. "no storage ABI qualification: run scripts/audit-storage-interface.py or provide the
recorded audit".

[unixnu-issue-storage-abi.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33962639/unixnu-issue-storage-abi.md)

issues.title: Stringsdict: all Russian plural entries are dropped on save, so the file is emptied and edits are never committed
issues.body:
### Describe the issue

On a **Stringsdict file** (`stringsdict`) component, saving the Russian translation writes an empty `<dict/>`. Every plural entry is dropped, including fully translated ones. The translations stay in the Weblate database, but they never reach the repository.

- File format: **Stringsdict file** (`stringsdict`), monolingual.
  - Base file: `<dir>/en.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`
  - File mask: `<dir>/*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`
- All entries are simple single-variable plurals (`NSStringLocalizedFormatKey` = `%#@count@`, one `NSStringPluralRuleType` dictionary).
- Add-ons on the component: `weblate.autotranslate.autotranslate`. The component is linked to the main component (`weblate://<project>/<component>`).
- Languages: de, es, fr, it, ja, ko, pt_BR, ru, zh_Hans, zh_Hant. **Only `ru` is affected.** The others save and commit normally.

What we observe:

1. A Weblate commit replaced our Russian file, which had 21 translated entries, with an empty dict:
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
   <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
   <plist version="1.0">
   <dict/>
   </plist>
   ```
   The commit message was "Translated using Weblate (Russian) – Currently translated at 100.0%".
2. Since then, **Download translation → original format** gives the empty file above, while **Download → CSV** contains all Russian plural translations (it is generated from the database).
3. Editing a Russian string in the UI and committing produces no commit and no push. The written file is the same empty dict every time, so git has nothing to commit and no pull request is updated.

#### Root cause

The bug is in translate-toolkit's `StringsDictFile.serialize()` (`translate/storage/stringsdict.py`). It was introduced in translate-toolkit **3.19.19** by commit `3367ed4a` ("fix(stringsdict): fold simple plural entries"), which fixed #21294:

```python
plural_tags = self._get_target_plural_tags(unit.target)
...
# Omit an untranslated or incomplete entry instead of writing
# a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime.
if (
    "other" not in plural_tags
    or not plural_strings[plural_tags.index("other")]
):
    continue
```

`plural_tags` comes from `translate.lang.data.plural_tags`. For `ru` (and also `pl`, `uk`, `be`) it is `["one", "few", "many"]`, and `_get_target_plural_tags()` adds `"zero"`, giving `['zero', 'one', 'few', 'many']`. **`"other"` is never in that list, so the condition is always true and every entry is skipped,** however complete the translation is.

The previous serializer wrote these entries correctly. Our Russian file round-tripped through Weblate for over a year before this change.

#### Proposed fix (translate-toolkit)

For languages without an `other` category, use the last category as the required fallback:

```diff
--- a/translate/storage/stringsdict.py
+++ b/translate/storage/stringsdict.py
@@ -288,11 +288,11 @@ class StringsDictFile(base.DictStore):
 
                 # Omit an untranslated or incomplete entry instead of writing
-                # a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime.
-                if (
-                    "other" not in plural_tags
-                    or not plural_strings[plural_tags.index("other")]
-                ):
+                # a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime. Languages
+                # such as Russian have no integer "other" category, their last
+                # category is the fallback instead.
+                fallback_tag = "other" if "other" in plural_tags else plural_tags[-1]
+                if not plural_strings[plural_tags.index(fallback_tag)]:
                     continue
```

Regression test, in the style of the existing `tests/translate/storage/test_stringsdict.py`:

```python
def test_single_plural_without_other_category(self) -> None:
    content = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>items</key>
    <dict>
        <key>NSStringLocalizedFormatKey</key>
        <string>%#@count@</string>
        <key>count</key>
        <dict>
            <key>NSStringFormatSpecTypeKey</key>
            <string>NSStringPluralRuleType</string>
            <key>NSStringFormatValueTypeKey</key>
            <string>d</string>
            <key>one</key>
            <string>%d элемент</string>
            <key>few</key>
            <string>%d элемента</string>
            <key>many</key>
            <string>%d элементов</string>
        </dict>
    </dict>
</dict>
</plist>"""
    store = self.StoreClass()
    store.settargetlanguage("ru")
    store.parse(content.encode())

    assert store.units[0].target.strings == [
        "",
        "%d элемент",
        "%d элемента",
        "%d элементов",
    ]
    output = plistlib.loads(bytes(store))["items"]["count"]
    assert output["one"] == "%d элемент"
    assert output["many"] == "%d элементов"

    store.units[0].target = multistring(["", "%d элемент", "%d элемента", ""])
    assert plistlib.loads(bytes(store)) == {}
```

The last assertion keeps the intent of #21294: an entry whose fallback form is empty is still omitted.

An alternative would be to also emit an `other` key for these languages (CLDR uses `other` for fractional values in ru/pl/uk/be). That would change the number of plural forms shown in Weblate, so the change above is the minimal one.

#### Verified vs not verified

- Verified:
  - With translate-toolkit 3.20.1 (pinned by Weblate 2026.10.1), saving a translated Russian unit writes an empty dict.
  - The new test fails on unpatched code (`KeyError: 'items'`) and passes with the patch. The whole `test_stringsdict.py` suite passes (44 tests).
  - With the patched file installed in a `weblate==2026.10.1` environment, `StringsdictFormat` with our real `en` template and the empty `ru` file writes the Russian entry with its `one`, `few` and `many` forms.
  - translate-toolkit `main` at `888e46cc` (2026-10-29) still has the same check.
- Not verified:
  - Polish, Ukrainian and Belarusian; they are inferred from `translate.lang.data.plural_tags`.
  - The full Weblate test suite with the patch.
  - Apple runtime behaviour with a Russian dict without `other`. It worked in our app before 3.19.19.

### I already tried

- [x] I've read and searched [the documentation](https://docs.weblate.org/).
- [x] I've searched for similar filed issues in this repository.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

**In the UI**

1. Create a monolingual **Stringsdict file** component with base `en.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict` and file mask `*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`.
2. Add a Russian translation `ru.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict` with a complete simple plural entry (`one`/`few`/`many`). The **Standalone** example below has one.
3. Edit any Russian string in the editor and save.
4. Manage → Repository maintenance → Commit, or Files → Download translation (original format).
5. The Russian file is now `<dict/>`, and all entries are gone. After that, further Russian edits never produce a commit.

**Standalone (translate-toolkit only, no Weblate server)**

```python
# uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with "translate-toolkit==3.20.1" python repro.py
import plistlib
from translate.storage.stringsdict import StringsDictFile

content = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>items</key><dict>
    <key>NSStringLocalizedFormatKey</key><string>%#@count@</string>
    <key>count</key><dict>
      <key>NSStringFormatSpecTypeKey</key><string>NSStringPluralRuleType</string>
      <key>NSStringFormatValueTypeKey</key><string>d</string>
      <key>one</key><string>%d элемент</string>
      <key>few</key><string>%d элемента</string>
      <key>many</key><string>%d элементов</string>
    </dict>
  </dict>
</dict></plist>"""

store = StringsDictFile()
store.settargetlanguage("ru")
store.parse(content.encode())
print(store._get_target_plural_tags(store.units[0].target))  # ['zero', 'one', 'few', 'many']
print(plistlib.loads(bytes(store)))                          # {}  <- entry dropped
```

Changing `settargetlanguage("ru")` to `"de"` (with `one`/`other` keys) writes the entry correctly.

### Expected behavior

A complete Russian (or Polish, Ukrainian, Belarusian) plural entry is written to the file, as it was before translate-toolkit 3.19.19. Only an entry whose fallback form is empty should be omitted, which was the intent of #21294.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Exception traceback

```pytb

```

### How do you run Weblate?

weblate.org service

### Weblate version

2026.10.1 (translate-toolkit 3.20.1)

### Weblate deploy checks

```shell

```

### Additional context

- Introduced by translate-toolkit commit `3367ed4a` "fix(stringsdict): fold simple plural entries", released in **3.19.19** (2026-09-01) and present in 3.20.0, 3.20.1 and `main`. It was a follow-up to #21294.
- The wrong language data is in `translate/lang/data.py` → `plural_tags["ru"] == ["one", "few", "many"]` (same for `pl`, `uk`, `be`). `DECIMAL_EXTRA_TAGS` in the same file lists `other` for these languages, but `_get_target_plural_tags()` doesn't use it.
- Impact: every Russian translation edit made in Weblate is silently kept out of the repository, and the first such commit wipes the existing Russian file. The only workaround is to maintain the Russian `.stringsdict` directly in the repository and avoid editing Russian in Weblate.
- Related: #21294.

issues.title: Add extraction scheme for Flarum forums
issues.body:
Flarum forums answer a JSON:API endpoint, and a scheme for it is a short one — a good place to start if you have not touched this repository before.

The endpoint is `{forum}/api/users?filter[q]={name}`. Verified on 2026-09-11: `https://forum.android.com.pl/api/users?filter[q]=rammiro` returns `data[0]` with `id` 3 and an `attributes` object holding the username, display name, join date and avatar URL. Twenty of the sites in [maigret's database](https://github.com/soxoj/maigret) run Flarum.

**What to extract:** `uid` and `username` at minimum, plus what maps onto [FIELDS.md](FIELDS.md) — `fullname`, `image`, `created_at`.

**Where to start:** schemes live in `socid_extractor/schemes.py`. `Discourse API` is the closest model. Note that this endpoint is a *search*, so `data` can hold several users or none — take the exact match, not the first element.

**Watch out for:** some instances refuse anonymous API calls. `https://forum.exbo.net/api/users?filter[q]=anyone` answers 403. The scheme should come back empty there rather than break.

**Done when:** an offline test in `tests/test_extended_schemes.py` passes against a saved JSON response — no live request, no cookies needed. A live test in `tests/test_e2e.py` with the docstring matching the scheme name is welcome on top of it.

**Size:** an hour.

issues.title: RG CubeXX: 32-bit box86 ports (Shovel Knight) get no gamepad input; keyboard via gptokeyb works as a fallback
issues.body:
### Bug report code

_No response_

### Device

Anbernic RG CubeXX

### spruce version

4.5.4

### What happened?

Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove (PortMaster, runs under box86) launches, but the pad is unresponsive apart from the Menu button. 

What I checked:
- SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG is set correctly and contains the pad (ANBERNIC-keys, GUID 19000000010000000100000000010000, valid a/b/x/y/shoulder/start/dpad/stick mappings).
- The port's shovelknight.gptk is intentionally empty (every line is \"), so input is meant to come from the game's own SDL2 reading the pad natively.
- The game is a 32-bit process, so the 64-bit entries in LD_LIBRARY_PATH (spruce/h700/lib64/sdl2, PyUI/dll-mali) don't apply. The only 32-bit SDL2 on the system library path is /usr/lib32/libSDL2-2.0.so.0.
- Tried adding /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/h700/lib32 to the front of LD_LIBRARY_PATH with the empty gptk: native pad input still didn't work.
- A one-time device freeze occurred on the first launch of this port; not reproduced since.

Workaround that works:
1. Populated shovelknight.gptk with keyboard mappings (d-pad and left stick to W/A/S/D, a/x to K for jump, b/y to J for attack, start to Enter, back to Esc).
2. Added `pm_platform_helper "$GAMEDIR/box86/box86" >/dev/null` to Shovel Knight.sh after the gptokeyb line, so SDL is pointed at gptokeyb's virtual keyboard through SDL_EVDEV_DEVICES. The stock script doesn't call it.
The game is fully playable this way.

Suggestion:
32-bit box86 ports need either a 32-bit SDL2 that exposes the pad natively, or pm_platform_helper called by default so the gptokeyb keyboard fallback works. Other box86 ports are likely affected too.

issues.title: [Bug] GKA FP32 with K > 64 doesn't fit in 99 KB shared memory
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have checked [FAQs](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/main/FAQs.md) and existing issues for similar problems
- [x] Please report this bug in English to ensure wider understanding and support

### Describe the Bug

On GPUs with 99 KB of shared memory per block (SM86/SM89, and RTX-class Blackwell SM120), GKA in FP32 with `K > 64` fails with `OutOfResources` in both directions:

- forward: `chunk_gka_solve_fwd_kernel`
- backward: `chunk_gka_bwd_kernel_dk_intra`, even when split into `PART=1`/`PART=2` (Required: 147456, Hardware limit: 101376)

With `BK=128` a single `[BK, BK]` FP32 tile of the state is already 64 KB, so I don't think tuning `num_warps`/`num_stages` can get it under 99 KB. It probably needs the `[K, K]` state blocked along K. bf16/fp16 and FP32 with `K <= 64` are fine once the backward is split into the existing `PART=1`/`PART=2` launches, and I'm opening a separate PR for that part.

H100 CI doesn't catch this since it has 227 KB per block.

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from fla.ops.gka import chunk_gka

for K in (64, 128):
    B, T, H, V = 2, 256, 4, K
    q = F.normalize(torch.randn(B, T, H, K, device='cuda'), p=2, dim=-1)
    k = F.normalize(torch.randn(B, T, H, K, device='cuda'), p=2, dim=-1)
    v = torch.randn(B, T, H, V, device='cuda')
    g = torch.empty(B, T, H, device='cuda').uniform_(0.8, 0.99).log()
    try:
        o = chunk_gka(q, k, v, g=g, gk=g)  # float32 inputs
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        print(f"K={K}: ok")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"K={K}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

On an RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (main @ f2ca71c0):

```
K=64: ok
K=128: OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 147456, Hardware limit: 101376. Reducing block sizes or `num_stages` may help.
```

These tests in `tests/ops/test_gka.py` fail the same way:

```
test_chunk_fwd[B2-T1024-H4-K128-V128-tied-alphaFalse-h0True-torch.float32]
test_chunk_fwd[B2-T256-H4-K100-V64-none-alphaTrue-h0False-torch.float32]
test_chunk_varlen_fwd[H4-K100-g_only-cu_seqlens[0, 256, 500, 1000]-torch.float32]
test_chunk_bwd[B2-T256-H4-K128-V128-tied-alphaFalse-h0True-torch.float32]
test_chunk_bwd[B2-T256-H4-K100-V64-none-alphaTrue-h0True-torch.float32]
test_chunk_varlen_bwd[H4-K100-g_only-cu_seqlens[0, 200, 256, 500]-torch.float32]
test_chunk_state_chaining[B2-T300-H4-K100-g_only-split37]
test_fused_recurrent_decode_after_chunk_prefill[B2-T80-H4-K128-g_only-prefill64]
```

### Expected Behavior

FP32 GKA with `K > 64` runs on GPUs with 99 KB of shared memory per block, like it does on H100, or fails with a clear error saying FP32 with `K > 64` needs more shared memory.

### Environment Information

1. Torch: 2.16.0.dev20261030+cu132
2. Triton: 3.9.0

Platform: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 101376 B shared memory per block), driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.2, Python 3.12.13, Linux. fla built from source at main @ f2ca71c0.

issues.title: NEMA: lagging left turn is never served in coordinated mode
issues.body:
**Problem**

In coordinated mode, a left turn that lags its coordinated phase is never served. With ring1 `2,1,0,4`, ring2 `5,6,0,8` and coordinated phases 2,6 (phase 1 lags phase 2, a common lead-lag plan), a called phase 1 never turns green and its vehicles wait until they teleport.

The controller assumes the coordinated phases are the last phases on their side of the barrier. That holds only when both lefts lead:

- `constructTimingAndPhaseDefs` (NEMAController.cpp:181, v1_28_0, unchanged on main) makes every coordinated phase a barrier phase.
- `fromCoord` (:1783) then waits for the other ring before any transition out of a coordinated phase, including the same-side 2 → 1.

**Repro** (attached zip, details in its README; TS2, cycle 100, one phase-1 vehicle from t=90 and one from t=363). In the unzipped folder:

```
sumo -n net.net.xml -r routes.rou.xml -a detectors.add.xml,tls.add.xml --end 600 --tripinfo-output tripinfo.xml
```

1.28.0: phase 1 is never green; the first vehicle waits until the default 300 s time-to-teleport runs out (`Warning: Teleporting vehicle 'lag1_called'; waited too long (yield), lane='1si_1', time=393.00.`), and the second doesn't arrive within the run. The same plan also shows a TS2 cycle-zero error: phases 2/6 turn green at 80, 180, … instead of 100, 200, …, because 1.28 puts the zero at phase 6's start.

**Proposed fix**

I have a patch with tests, against 1.28.0; its code applies to main unchanged. It takes each ring's barrier phase from the ring order (the last phase on each side), so lead/lag is set by ring order alone, with no new parameter. In coordinated mode:

- A called lag runs after its coordinated phase's force-off, alongside the other ring's coordinated phase, and ends by its own force-off. A call that no longer fits waits for the next cycle.
- An uncalled lag's split goes to its coordinated phase, which holds to the barrier.
- A lag that gaps out keeps its green until the side street is called, or until the coordinated phase's next start.

Plans whose coordinated phases are last on their side are unchanged: all existing NEMA texttests pass unmodified. The repro then gives no warnings, phases 2/6 green at 100, 200, …, and arrivals at 195 and 500.

One design choice I'd like your view on: a lag that gaps out with no side-street demand keeps its green to the coordinated phase's next start, so that through movement waits up to about 40 s. The alternative is to return to the coordinated phase early and let it yield to a later side-street call after its minimum green. Real controllers offer both.

Would you welcome a PR? I'd sign the ECA first. It would include a `tls/NEMA/lagging_left` texttest suite and a NEMA.md section. I also found a few pre-existing start-up and Type 170 timing quirks while testing, and can report those separately.

**SUMO-version:** 1.28.0 (official eclipse-sumo wheel; the NEMA controller source on main is unchanged since 1.28.0)

**operating system:** macOS (Apple silicon)

[lagging-left-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34147242/lagging-left-repro.zip)

ENH:  DataFrame.merge raises bare KeyError without saying which DataFrame is missing the key column
issues.body:
### Feature Type

- [ ] Adding new functionality to pandas

- [x] Changing existing functionality in pandas

- [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas


### Problem Description

When a key column passed to `on=` (or `left_on` / `right_on`) is missing from one of the DataFrames, `merge` raises a bare KeyError containing only the column name. It doesn't say which DataFrame (left or right) is missing the column, or which columns are available.

import pandas as pd

orders = pd.DataFrame({"customer_id": [1, 2, 3], "amount": [10, 20, 30]})
customers = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["A", "B", "C"]})

orders.merge(customers, on="customer_id")

Actual:
KeyError: 'customer_id'

The traceback ends in pandas/core/generic.py (_get_label_or_level_values), reached via _get_merge_keys in pandas/core/reshape/merge.py. I saw the same bare KeyError on pandas 2.3.3 and 3.0.2, with on="id" (missing on the left), on="zzz" (missing on both), and with typos in left_on / right_on.

With on=, the column must exist in both frames, so the user has to inspect both DataFrames to find the cause.

### Feature Description

Raise a more informative error, for example:

KeyError: "'customer_id' not found in right DataFrame. Available columns: ['id', 'name']"

Other merge errors already name the dtypes on both sides ("You are trying to merge on int64 and str columns for key 'k'"), so this would be consistent. One possible place is where _get_merge_keys calls _get_label_or_level_values: catch the KeyError and re-raise it with the side and available columns.

### Alternative Solutions

Users can print left.columns and right.columns before merging, but the error message itself should say where the key is missing.

### Additional Context

The existing test in pandas/tests/reshape/merge/test_join.py expects the bare KeyError (match="^'E'$" for join(on="E")), so it would need updating together with the message.

Related: #65553 (closed) asked for a more descriptive KeyError for df["Age"] and was closed as fine as-is. This request is specifically about merge, where there are two DataFrames. With df["Age"] it's obvious which object lacks the column, but with merge(on="customer_id") the bare KeyError can't tell the user whether the left or the right frame is missing it. If maintainers feel the same reasoning applies here, I understand and am happy for this to be closed.

issues.title: Compatibility: support modern union syntax for type hints and introspection
issues.body:
Hi there! First of all, thank you for maintaining `watchfiles`. It's a fantastic library that powers our development workflows smoothly.

While working with type hints and runtime schema reflection under Python 3.10+, I noticed a few spots where modern union syntax (`T | None`) interacts with older `typing.Union` structures. Ensuring type stubs and introspection utilities handle both formats cleanly helps avoid potential edge-case `TypeError` issues in modern environments.

### Environment
- Python version: 3.12.1
- Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
- Watchfiles version: Current main branch

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Inspect type annotations or pass custom callables utilizing modern union syntax (`int | None`) into type-checked utility wrappers.
2. Observe introspection tools attempting to parse the union representation.

### Expected Behavior
Both `typing.Union`/`typing.Optional` and modern PEP 604 union types (`|`) should be evaluated consistently by internal type-checking or introspection helpers without raising unexpected type errors.

### Actual Behavior
Some runtime type checks or introspection routines occasionally encounter unexpected representations when encountering native pipe unions.

Happy to submit a quick PR for this if the maintainers are open to it!

issues.title: Find devices on the network again without fetching Google's device list
issues.body:
glocaltokens' `get_google_devices()` fetches Google's device list and runs mDNS in one call, so finding a device's address again means asking Google again: #1079 does that every 10th update while a device has no address. The integration also redoes part of that call: it reads `homegraph` afterwards to name devices as Google does and to get their cloud device IDs ([`api.py`](https://github.com/leikoilja/ha-google-home/blob/5e1236f890b025c07a2262bf2c63b45036d5d202/custom_components/google_home/api.py#L127-L155)).

Proposal: call the two parts that glocaltokens already exposes.

- `get_homegraph()` at setup and after a device rejects its token, for the devices with their tokens, names and cloud device IDs.
- `glocaltokens.scanner.discover_devices()` and the known hosts on any update where a device has no address or didn't answer. Match both by cloud device ID, as known hosts already are: mDNS reports it as `cd`. mDNS takes about 2 seconds and sends nothing to Google.

A device that comes back online is then found at the next update without a request to Google. Related: #122, #1079.

issues.title: Crash with --set-exif-datetime: uncaught struct.error from piexif on malformed EXIF
issues.body:
## Summary

With `--set-exif-datetime`, icloudpd crashes when a downloaded photo has a truncated or malformed EXIF block. `piexif.load()` raises `struct.error`. `get_photo_exif` / `set_photo_exif` in `src/icloudpd/exif_datetime.py` catch only `ValueError` and `InvalidImageDataError`, so `struct.error` goes uncaught and the whole run aborts.

This is the same symptom as #411 (closed for lack of a repro; a reproducer image was attached afterwards in that thread). The underlying piexif bug is hMatoba/Piexif#129.

## Version

icloudpd 1.32.3 (Homebrew, Python 3.14, macOS)

## Traceback

```
  File ".../icloudpd/base.py", line 716, in download_builder
    and not exif_datetime.get_photo_exif(logger, download_path)
  File ".../icloudpd/exif_datetime.py", line 13, in get_photo_exif
    exif_dict: piexif.ExifIFD = piexif.load(path)
  File ".../piexif/_load.py", line 53, in load
    exif_dict["1st"] = exifReader.get_ifd_dict(pointer, "1st")
  File ".../piexif/_load.py", line 129, in get_ifd_dict
    ifd_dict[tag] = self.convert_value(v_set)
  File ".../piexif/_load.py", line 188, in convert_value
    data = (struct.unpack(self.endian_mark + "L",
struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of 4 bytes
```

## Suggested fix

Even without fixing or replacing piexif, icloudpd could treat this like the errors it already handles: log and skip, rather than crash.

```diff
 import logging
+import struct
 import typing
@@
-    except (ValueError, InvalidImageDataError):
+    except (ValueError, InvalidImageDataError, struct.error):
         logger.debug("Error fetching EXIF data for %s", path)
@@
-    except (ValueError, InvalidImageDataError):
+    except (ValueError, InvalidImageDataError, struct.error):
         logger.debug("Error setting EXIF data for %s", path)
```

I applied this patch locally and the module loads fine.
