issues.title: yue2_infer 0.1.5: CUDA graph refused on the FP8 AR path — small patch, 4.5× faster composing on an 8 GB GPU (+ 2 Windows/FP8 findings)
issues.body:
Hi.

**Problem.** `yue2_infer` 0.1.5 always falls back to the eager decode loop when the AR weights are FP8 (`GraphAR only supports unquantized standard AR Linear layers; use eager for FP8`). On consumer 8 GB cards FP8 is the only way to run YuE2-3B, so those users never get the CUDA graph.

**Change.** Two small hunks (patch linked below) let `GraphAR` accept the `FP8Linear` modules that the eager path already uses; `generate_tokens` takes the graph path for FP8 when `YUE2_GRAPH=1`. Default behaviour unchanged.

**Measured** (RTX 5060 Laptop 8 GB, Windows 11, torch 2.10.0+cu128, YuE2-3B rev `8f24312`, VAE rev `152733a`, one song, single runs):

| | eager | FP8 CUDA graph (cuDNN attention) |
|---|---|---|
| Lab script, song stage (AR) | 4120 tok in 439.0 s — 9.4 tok/s | 4000 tok in 76.5 s — 52.3 tok/s (5.6×) |
| Lab script, plan stage | 1578 tok in 127.0 s — 12.4 tok/s | 1635 tok in 28.5 s — 57.4 tok/s (4.6×) |
| UNICA runner, plan+song end to end | 3648 tok in 477.9 s — 0.131 s/tok | 3047 tok in 87.1 s — 0.0286 s/tok (**4.58×**) |
| UNICA runner, same seed 8, back to back | 3648 tok in 648.4 s — 0.178 s/tok | 3997 tok in 120.3 s — 0.0301 s/tok (**5.9×**) |
| Peak VRAM, AR stage | 6.88 GB | 6.74–7.03 GB |
| Load / NAR 4 steps / VAE | 6.7 s / 42.0 s / 6.4 s | 5.8 s / 28.8 s / 5.3 s |

Full stage-by-stage tables, exact revisions, `pip freeze`, reproduction commands, before/after logs, the patch and the benchmark scripts are here:
https://github.com/umbertomaravigna61-debug/unica/tree/main/contrib/yue2-fp8-cuda-graph

**Output / stability.** Five complete graph runs, no errors, audio normal. Each path is deterministic with a fixed seed (eager seed 8 gave exactly 3648 tokens on two different days), but the two paths are not identical to each other: in a same-seed A/B they diverge at the second token (3648 vs 3997 tokens; 0.2 % position-wise equal), as expected from a different attention kernel under sampling. A signal analysis of that pair (loudness, true peak, crest factor, band energy, spectrograms, chroma) finds the two outputs technically equivalent — same tempo candidates, loudness within 0.5 LU, chroma similarity 0.91, no artefacts; the only true-peak overshoot is on the eager side. Tables, plots and the listening verdict are in the write-up, §5d–5e.

**Two independent findings while doing this:**
1. `attention_backend="auto"` selects FlashAttention on the official Windows torch 2.10.0+cu128 build (the `hasattr`/schema test passes) but the first capture fails with `USE_FLASH_ATTENTION was not enabled for build`. Forcing `cudnn` works. Log in the folder.
2. `nar._offload_ar` raises `generator raised StopIteration` with FP8 weights (it looks for a parameter; `FP8Linear` only has buffers). A version that checks `parameters()` and `buffers()` works.

Happy to turn this into a PR against whatever repository holds the `yue2_infer` source (the wheel on Hugging Face does not point to one), and to run any additional measurement you find useful.

Umberto Maravigna (UNICA)

issues.title: Ruach Studio 2.0.0 is out: a free studio around YuE2-3B, and YuE2-RS-FW, a fine-tune of it as merged weights
issues.body:
Hello m-a-p, and thank you again for YuE2. Our studio is built around it.

**[Ruach Studio 2.0.0](https://github.com/igrbible/Ruach_Studio/releases/tag/v2.0.0)** is out, its first stable release. It is a free, open studio that runs YuE2 on your own hardware through [yue2.cpp](https://github.com/ServeurpersoCom/yue2.cpp): Linux with an NVIDIA card, Windows through WSL2, Intel Arc as a beta. The model, the score, the adapters and every take stay on your machine. Six rooms as one:
- the **Creator** writes and edits songs as YuE2 plans them: Full mode with the score, Only the opening, Extend, re-singing a line, a section or a window, chords and a chord bed, and a piano roll for YuE2's ABC scores (beta);
- the **Writer**, a lyrics room with a language model of your choice;
- the **Refiner**, a canvas of nodes from eight stems to mastering, with a DAW (beta);
- the **Artist**, for covers;
- the **Librarian**, with a playlist;
- the **Trainer**, LoRA training for YuE2 on one card or several.

The guide is in twelve languages.

**[YuE2-RS-FW](https://huggingface.co/goldhub/YuE2-RS-Finetunes)** is our first fine-tune of YuE2-3B, the First Wave, published only as merged weights. Each merge comes as GGUF (BF16, Q8_0, Q6_K) and as BF16 safetensors in your own layout, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with credit to YuE2-3B.
- **Data:** 32,633 tracks, about 1,800 hours. MTG-Jamendo and FMA above an Audiobox Aesthetics bar (PQ ≥ 7.0), two community sets of songs with lyrics, and a guard of sung and spoken material. 31,801 tracks have their own ABC score (SheetSage2), so Full mode is trained too.
- **Training:** LoRA on both halves (music half rank 160, sound half rank 320), four epochs, EMA, three RTX 3090s.
- **Merges:** seven checkpoint and strength pairs. Ruach Studio takes 2.4 × 0.75 as its default for now; the blind listening that picks the best one is under way.

**Findings that may interest you:**
- **A later save weighs more.** Measured as the norm of what a save adds, the change grows about 3× on the music half and 2.5× on the sound half from epoch 0.7 to 4.0. At one strength, a late save pushes much harder, so we merge later saves lighter.
- **The music half keeps its scores.** 320 plans in Full mode (20 cards × saves 0.7–4.0 × strengths 0.6–0.75) passed the score guard, none broken; a second seed at 0.75 gave 80 of 80 with a sung vocal line.
- **A grain on high female voices.** From about 1.5 epochs on, a fine grain (a «sand») comes back on high female voices, as we hear it in the stock weights; we are testing lighter strengths and a lighter sound half alone.
- **A ring against two closed services**, the same 20 cards (style and lyrics) sent to each, raw takes, one yardstick. The table is on the [model card](https://huggingface.co/goldhub/YuE2-RS-Finetunes).
  - On lyrics (Whisper's word error), the 0.7 save is at 18 % against 17 % and 23 % for the two closed services; the stock weights are at 21 %.
  - The 0.7 save measures the least sand of all five columns, and half the stray tones of the stock weights.
  - The decoder's 25 Hz frame buzz in the highs measures about 3 dB above the closed services in every YuE2 column, stock and fine-tuned alike. We thought you might want that number.

The merges and their measurements are on the model card. Questions and corrections are welcome.

Viktor Zhuromskyy and Ruach Studio

issues.title: Surface Pro X (SQ2, SC8180X): iPadOS boots and composites through Metal on Adreno 6xx; how should A6xx support land in Adreno740?
issues.body:
## Surface Pro X (Microsoft SQ2) community port, work in progress

UniXNU boots iPadOS 17.7.11 (21H461) to the SpringBoard home screen on a Surface Pro X. SpringBoard is composited through Metal on the device's Adreno GPU, using Adreno740, AdrenoMetal and Turnip, with an A6xx path added to the driver. The source is not public yet. This issue introduces the port, links the first upstream changes, and asks how you'd like the larger A6xx work structured before we send it.

**Tested device:** Surface Pro X (2020) with the **Microsoft SQ2** (Qualcomm SC8180X family). The GPU runs with Linux's sc8180x / A680 configuration: chip ID `0x06080001`, `a680_gmu.bin` and `a630_sqe.fw`, and the platform's zap shader. **SQ1 units have not been tested.** They are the same SoC family, but differences in clocks, firmware or GPU configuration have not been checked.

### What works on hardware

- **Boot.** The device boots from the internal ESP through its own EFI launcher. Windows remains the default boot entry. Each run is a full iPadOS boot to SpringBoard, which appears with the wallpaper, icons, dock and status bar. Keyboard input works through the Type Cover.
- **GPU bring-up through Adreno740's core**, using an SC8180X fork of the sm8550 platform kit for the A6xx GMU:
  - GMU cold start and HFI;
  - GX power;
  - the GPU SMMU context;
  - CP init on an A6xx ring, with CACHE_FLUSH_TS fences, RB_CNTL NO_UPDATE and CCU invalidates per submit;
  - `native_adreno_publish`.
- **Zap shader.** It loads through TrustZone PAS (INIT_IMAGE, MEM_SETUP, AUTH_AND_RESET), then `CP_SET_SECURE_MODE 0` leaves secure mode. Two findings:
  - MEM_SETUP is refused unless its size is page-aligned (`ALIGN(end, 4K) - start`, as in `qcom_mdt_pas_init`).
  - A direct `RBBM_SECVID_TRUST_CNTL = 0` write freezes this SoC.
- **Binning.** Turnip's GMEM binning works once the GPU is out of secure mode. In secure mode, the VSC writes never land and the CP waits forever.
- **SMMU.** The GPU and GMU routes need SMR masks: stream 0 mask 0xc01 and stream 5 mask 0xc00, from the Linux devicetree.

### Not working yet

- Performance is far from usable: about 100 ms per command buffer.
- Widgets render blank.
- Touch does not work.
- The stall recovery in Adreno740 is still A7xx-specific.

### Upstream changes so far

- UniXNU/ArmSmmu4K#3: SMR masks on stream routes.
- UniXNU/Adreno740#7: companion initializer update.
- UniXNU/UniXNU#120: docs.

### Questions

1. **A6xx in Adreno740.** The A6xx differences are small, but they cut through ring/fence emission, hardware init, IRQ masks and the stall handling. We currently select A6xx with a global mode switch. Would you prefer a per-GPU generation/ops field in Adreno740, or a separate A6xx driver that shares the user-client and VM core?
2. **SoC repository.** Should the A6xx GMU/HFI kit (the sm8550 platform kit API with A6xx registers, RSC/PDC setup and SC8180X votes) live in a new `UniXNU-sc8180x-common`?
3. **Device listing.** We'd like to publish the device repository and ask for a community listing once the source is out. Is there anything specific you want in the validation record?

issues.title: Proposal: Register reusable Mali CSF and MaliMetal GPU acceleration components
issues.body:
# Proposal: Register reusable Mali CSF and MaliMetal GPU acceleration components

## Summary

I would like to contribute reusable Mali GPU acceleration components to UniXNU and discuss their integration into the official component catalog.

My Rockchip RK3588 EVB10 V10 port runs iPadOS 17.7.11 (21H461) with hardware-accelerated Metal rendering on the Mali-G610 MC4.

The graphics pipeline is:

`SpringBoard / backboardd → NativeMaliMetal → metal2vulkan → Mesa PanVK → Darwin DRM compatibility → Mali IOKit driver → Mali-G610 CSF`

## Hardware verification

- iPadOS boots into SpringBoard.
- The DSI panel displays the interface and the Goodix touchscreen works.
- Metal rendering is accelerated by the Mali GPU, rather than a software framebuffer.
- Home-screen scrolling reaches 52.6 FPS on average and 57.5 FPS at best in the documented scripted tests.
- Stable 60 FPS remains an optimization target.
- The complete source was rebuilt and booted on October 29, 2026. Panel and touch had been validated separately, but were not visually rechecked during that particular rebuild test.

## Public repositories

- [[Mali](https://github.com/Ken-u/Mali)](https://github.com/Ken-u/Mali) — XNU/IOKit Mali CSF kernel driver.
- [[MaliMetal](https://github.com/Ken-u/MaliMetal)](https://github.com/Ken-u/MaliMetal) — Metal plug-in, Vulkan bridge, PanVK, Darwin DRM compatibility and Mesa patches.
- [[UniXNU-rk3588-common](https://github.com/Ken-u/UniXNU-rk3588-common)](https://github.com/Ken-u/UniXNU-rk3588-common) — Shared RK3588 SoC support.
- [[UniXNU-evb10](https://github.com/Ken-u/UniXNU-evb10)](https://github.com/Ken-u/UniXNU-evb10) — Board integration, display, touch and porting records.
- [[Reproduction guide](https://github.com/Ken-u/UniXNU-evb10/blob/main/docs/reproduce.md)](https://github.com/Ken-u/UniXNU-evb10/blob/main/docs/reproduce.md) — Clean rebuild and boot procedure.

## Proposed upstream structure

1. **Mali:** A reusable XNU IOKit GPU driver component, with SoC-specific power, clock and firmware integration separated out.
2. **MaliMetal:** A Mali-specific Metal/Vulkan backend, including the PanVK and Darwin compatibility layers.
3. **Shared Metal frontend:** Reuse common functionality from the existing AdrenoMetal/NativeMetal work where practical.
4. **Mesa patches:** Submit general-purpose PanVK improvements upstream separately.

The existing implementation has only been verified on RK3588/Mali-G610. Other Mali GPUs would require additional development and validation.

Existing third-party licenses and source attribution will be preserved.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Would you accept Mali and MaliMetal as reusable components in the official `components.toml` catalog?
2. Should MaliMetal initially remain an independent component, or should its common frontend be consolidated with the existing Metal implementation?
3. Would you prefer integration using the current community repositories, or should the code be refactored before registration?
4. What additional validation, build metadata or documentation would be required?

I would prefer to agree on the component boundaries before moving repositories or making large structural changes.

Related discussion: #121 (Adreno 6xx GPU support).

issues.title: Support for central authentication system
issues.body:
In order for Conpot to look more realistic to attackers, there should be a central authentication system that provides more consistency. Protocols should be able to query this auth module and verify the user/pass pairs.

**_Requirements:_**
- Pick user/pass pairs from the config. 
- A Utility to add a pair of credentials to our auth data structure.
- Utility to check the whether the passed user/pass exists in our Data Structure
- Maintain 'maxcache' for the number of attempts from each source IP. If the attempts exceed the 'maxcache', return False.
- A random auth class that also tracks source IP address
- Every new source IP will have to try a random number of times between 'mintry' and 'maxtry' before succeeding to login.
- All username/password combinations must be different.
- The successful login combination is stored with the IP address.
- Successful username/passwords pairs are also cached for 'maxcache' times.
- Allow access from different IP addresses if a credential pair is accepted.
- Protocols can use either local scope or global scope to authenticate. For eg: FTP user 'Anonymous` does not exist with any other protocol. Hence should be kept separate 

This should be a core feature and part of the databus. Further all existing protocols must be refactored to use this e.g: FTP, SNMP, IPMI etc. 

**_Nice to have:_**

- Every user can have a home directory in the ConpotFS.
- Support for multiple hashing algorithms. This can be optional. But it would be cool if users can directly attach rainbow tables to Conpot
- Check and verify using popular brute-forcing tools.

issues.title: OPC UA: FileType / file transfer capture
issues.body:
## Summary

Extend the OPC UA honeypot (see [#82](https://github.com/mushorg/conpot/issues/82), [#650](https://github.com/mushorg/conpot/pull/650)) to support **OPC UA FileType** objects and capture file transfer activity from clients.

The baseline `opcua` protocol ships with a Plant address space and SecurityPolicy **None** only. FileType transfer was explicitly deferred.

## Motivation

OPC UA is commonly used for device file transfer (firmware, configs, logs). Capturing uploads/downloads — and linking artifacts to attack sessions — was part of the original [#82](https://github.com/mushorg/conpot/issues/82) intent:

> storing any files to a separate directory and create an md5 entry in the data section of the log entry so we are able to link it back to the attacker.

## Proposed scope

- Expose one or more template-configured **FileType** nodes (or a folder of files) in the address space
- Handle FileType method calls clients use for transfer (`Open` / `Read` / `Write` / `Close` / `GetPosition` / `SetPosition`, as applicable via asyncua)
- Persist transferred payloads under a dedicated capture directory (honeypot VFS or a protocol-local path — follow existing FTP/TFTP patterns where sensible)
- Log session events for file operations, including **MD5** (and size / path / mode) so artifacts can be correlated with the attacker session
- Bound sizes / timeouts so untrusted clients cannot stall workers or fill disk unbounded
- Template/schema knobs for enabling FileType nodes, initial decoy content, and capture limits
- Tests + docs updates (`docs/source/protocols/opcua.rst`)

## Out of scope (unless needed later)

- Sign/Encrypt security policies
- Proxying file ops to a live PLC
- Full historical access / complex RolePermissions modeling beyond what FileType needs

## References

- Current docs note FileType as out of scope: `docs/source/protocols/opcua.rst`
- Implementation: `conpot/protocols/opcua/`
- OPC UA FileType (IEC 62541 Part 5 / companion File Transfer)

issues.title: [GPU] complex `sin` op results `nan`
issues.body:
### Summary 

This issue appears to be a partial manifestation of #781, the uninitialized GV issue.

### MRE
```python
import cmath
import gpu


@gpu.kernel
def kernel(xs, out_real, out_imag):
    z = cmath.sin(xs[0])
    out_real[0] = z.real
    out_imag[0] = z.imag


x = complex(0.5, 0.25)
cpu = cmath.sin(x)
out_real = [0.0]
out_imag = [0.0]

kernel([x], out_real, out_imag, grid=1, block=1)
gpu_result = complex(out_real[0], out_imag[0])

print("input:", x)
print("CPU cmath.sin:", cpu)
print("GPU cmath.sin:", gpu_result)
```

### results
```bash
$ codon run -release mre_complex_sin.codon 
input: (0.5+0.25j)
CPU cmath.sin: (0.494486+0.221688j)
GPU cmath.sin: (nan+nanj)
```

### Root Cause
For complex values, `cmath.sin` is not lowered to the primitive `sin(float)` operation directly. 

Instead, it is evaluated using the `Euler-based` complex formula:
```
For complex var C = a + bi
sin(C) = sin(a) * cosh(b) + i * cos(a) * sinh(b)
```
The CPU implementation appears to compute this correctly, while the GPU version returns `nan`.

In `cmath.codon`, the complex implementation uses GV-backed constants/functions:
```
    if math.fabs(z.real) > _CM_LOG_LARGE_DOUBLE:
        x_minus_one = z.real - math.copysign(1., z.real)
        r_real = math.cos(z.imag) * math.sinh(x_minus_one) * e
        r_imag = math.sin(z.imag) * math.cosh(x_minus_one) * e
    else:
        r_real = math.cos(z.imag) * math.sinh(z.real)
        r_imag = math.sin(z.imag) * math.cosh(z.real)
```

As discussed in #781, this seems likely to be caused by the `uninitialized GV issue`.

issues.title: Cannot import TYPE_CHECKING from `typing` / TYPE_CHECKING not ignored
issues.body:
Python static analysis fails on some codon-specific code (i.e. u32, u64 used as types). An handy solution could be including for the type checkers a small section where necessary, like:
```
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
if TYPE_CHECKING:
    u64 = int
    u32 = int
```
This should allow standard type checkers and static analysis to work decently with codon.

As of now, the above code results in the compilation error:
```
error: cannot import name 'TYPE_CHECKING' from 'typing'
```

A simple fix, I believe, would be adding `TYPE_CHECKING = False` in [typing](https://github.com/exaloop/codon/tree/master/stdlib/typing.codon)

EDIT: I am not sure the codon compiler skips entirely a block that is 100% sure not to be executed. If that's not the case, it might not be as easy :')

issues.title: feat(schema): honor conditional input requirements from model schemas
issues.body:
`scenario-sdk` 2.3.0 documents a fourth rule for when a model input is required, beside `always`, `ifDefined` and `ifNotDefined`:

```json
"required": { "conditional": { "values": { "<other input>": ["<value>", ...] }, "operator": "and" | "or" } }
```

The input is required when the named inputs hold one of the listed values; `operator` combines several conditions.

`_parse_required` in `scenario/core/schema/params.py` reads only `always`, `ifDefined` and `ifNotDefined`, so an input with a `conditional` rule is treated as optional. A user who sets the triggering value and leaves the input empty gets no requirement in the form, and the request is left for the service to reject.

To do:

- Parse `required.conditional` into the parameter spec, defaulting `operator` to the documented behavior.
- Apply it wherever the other requirement rules are applied today: the parameter controls (`params_ui.py`), render lanes and commands, `schema/forms.py` and the MCP tool schema (`tools_scenario.py`).
- Add schema tests for single and combined conditions.

Found while reviewing #638 (SDK 2.3.0 adoption), which does not change schema parsing.

However, when I click "Read saved Blockout plan", the following warning is displayed:
"Plan needs review: check job and destination."

The saved plan cannot be opened or reviewed, and I cannot proceed with applying the Blockout plan to my Blender scene.
Clicking "Inspect saved jobs" also produces no visible response.
The API connection test is successful, and Blender's Online Access is enabled.

Expected behavior:
The saved Blockout plan should open so that I can review its contents, confirm the destination and proceed with applying it to the scene.

Actual behavior:
The plan cannot be opened or reviewed, and no further action is possible.

Plugin panel or composer (UI, settings, import into the scene)

Select Exterior and District.

issues.title: Any plans for i18n? I added Korean support in my fork
issues.body:
I'm Korean, and using Open Executive in English was getting in the way for me, so I added i18n with Korean in my fork: https://github.com/y0ngha/OpenExecutive/tree/feat/korean-ui

How it works:

- One setting, OE_LANGUAGE (ENGLISH by default, or KOREAN), picks the language for the whole deployment at runtime. With it unset, the English UI is unchanged.
- Web UI: text is moved into per-area English/Korean dictionaries with a small t() helper, no new dependency. Pages render per request, so a prebuilt Docker image follows the setting.
- Model output: prompts stay in English. For Korean, one fixed system block is added after the cached blocks, so prompt caching still works. Words the code parses (YES/NO, JSON and so on) stay in English.
- API text and the user guide: fixed messages the API shows use a localized(english, korean) helper, and the guide has Korean copies with an English fallback.
- Playbook and knowledge content stays in English, since the models read it.

Do you have any plans to support i18n? If so, I'd be happy to open a PR, split into smaller pieces if that's easier to review.

/trading: comparison legend rows draw over the symbol's OHLC readout
issues.body:
## What happens

On `/trading`, add a comparison symbol and move the crosshair over the chart. The comparison's legend row is drawn in the chart's top-left corner, on top of the terminal's own OHLC readout next to the symbol name. The row shows the comparison symbol, its close and its change, and it updates with the crosshair. The two readouts overlap and neither can be read.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open `/trading` on any symbol.
2. Add a comparison symbol.
3. Hover over the chart.

## Expected

Comparison rows stack below the OHLC readout and the SELL/qty/BUY panel, the way indicator legend rows already do.

## Cause

- **The terminal keeps the corner clear.** `frontend/src/lib/trading/terminal.ts` creates the chart with `legendOffset: { top: 80 }`, so canvas legend rows start below the OHLC readout and the trade panel.
- **The chart offsets indicator rows only.** openalgo-charts applies `legendOffset` only to indicator rows. Rows a host adds keep their own `top`, by design ("Host-added legend rows are left alone: the host positions its own", `src/core/chart-legends.ts`).
- **The comparison row is a host row with no `top`.** `TerminalComparisons.addLegend` in `frontend/src/lib/trading/terminalComparisons.ts` creates each comparison's `PaneLegend` without one, so it takes the default 6 px and lands on the readout.

Seen on 2.0.2.9; the same code is on `main` (2.0.3.1). A fix follows in a PR.

issues.title: Strategy module: batch legs are capped at 50 lots, and no leg order is split at the freeze limit
issues.body:
## What happens

On `/strategy/new`, the **Lots** box of a batch leg will not go above 50. Typing a larger number silently turns it into 50, and nothing on the page says why. The server refuses anything above 50 too, so a strategy with, say, an 80-lot NIFTY leg cannot be built.

- UI: [`Wizard.tsx` L347-356](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/frontend/src/pages/strategy/Wizard.tsx#L347-L356) clamps the value with `Math.min(maxBatchQuantityFor(...), ...)`.
- Server: `MAX_LOTS = 50` in [`blueprints/strategy_module.py` L282](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/blueprints/strategy_module.py#L282), applied to derivative legs at [L642](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/blueprints/strategy_module.py#L642).

## Why raising the cap alone would not fix it

Each leg's entry and each leg's exit is sent as **one order**:

- The engine builds and dispatches a single order per leg, for entry ([`engine.py` L783](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/services/strategy_module/engine.py#L783)) and for exit ([L1392](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/services/strategy_module/engine.py#L1392)).
- Signal mode does the same ([`signals.py` L842](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/services/strategy_module/signals.py#L842)).
- Nothing in `services/strategy_module/` or `blueprints/strategy_module.py` reads the freeze table, and no broker plugin slices orders itself.

The index freeze limits in `data/qtyfreeze.csv` (#2218) work out to roughly 50 lots:

| Underlying | Freeze qty | Lot size | Freeze qty ÷ lot size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NIFTY | 3,510 | 65 | 54 |
| FINNIFTY | 3,240 | 60 | 54 |
| BANKNIFTY | 1,440 | 30 | 48 |
| MIDCPNIFTY | 5,760 | 120 | 48 |
| NIFTYNXT50 | 1,125 | 25 | 45 |

So with a higher cap and no splitting, the failure would only move from the form to the exchange.

## Related problems

1. **The clamp is silent.** The operator never learns there is a limit, or what it is.
2. **50 is already above the freeze for three indices.** A BANKNIFTY or MIDCPNIFTY leg of 49-50 lots, or a NIFTYNXT50 leg of 46-50 lots, passes validation and then goes to the exchange as one order above the freeze quantity.
3. **Signal legs allow up to 10,000 lots** (`MAX_SIGNAL_LOTS`, [L274](https://github.com/marketcalls/openalgo/blob/dd198ba99529fb13c20ef97fa1f58345fab170ea/blueprints/strategy_module.py#L274)) through the same single-order dispatch, so anything above the freeze fails there as well.

## Possible fix

- **Proper fix:** split a leg's entry and exit into freeze-sized child orders, then raise or drop `MAX_LOTS`. The freeze lookup (`get_freeze_qty_for_option`) and the slicing in `services/split_order_service.py` already exist; scalping exits use them. This does change the engine's one-order-per-leg model (order rows, acknowledgement, fill reconciliation, recovery), so it seems worth agreeing on the design before a PR.
- **Smaller step in the meantime:** cap each leg at `floor(freeze / lot size)` for its underlying when a freeze is known, and show the limit and the reason instead of clamping silently. That covers problems 1 and 2.

Seen on 2.0.2.9; the same code is on `main` (2.0.3.1, dd198ba9).

issues.title: WhatsApp: add an "observe" group mode that records all messages and lets the owner track questions
issues.body:
## What

Add an `observe` mode for WhatsApp groups, like the Slack channel's `observe` mode.

In this mode the agent stays silent in the group, but every message from every
member is recorded (not only messages from the owner and `allowed_wa_ids`).
The owner can then, from the self-chat or the dashboard:

- look back over recent group history ("what questions were asked this week?")
- have the agent find questions raised in the group and track their status
  (open / answered / follow-up needed)
- get a private notification (self-chat or dashboard) when a new question
  appears or an open one goes unanswered too long

The agent should never post in the group in this mode.

## Why

I use WhatsApp groups for customer technical support. I need to know which
questions were asked, who answered, and what is still open, without the bot
speaking in the group.

Today this is not possible:

- `group_gate.py`: messages from members not in `allowed_wa_ids` are dropped
  before reaching the agent.
- `transport.py`: `fetch_history` returns `[]`, and messages from before the
  connection are dropped, so there is no history to look back on.
- Turns triggered by other members run with no tools, so the agent cannot
  record a question or notify the owner privately.

Adding members to `allowed_wa_ids` is not a workaround: it lets them make the
agent reply in the group, which I do not want.

## Additional Context

- Platform: macOS, Kiro Crew desktop app
- Channel: WhatsApp (linked device via neonize), 3 groups configured
- Nice to have: a configurable history window, and a dashboard view of
  tracked questions per group.

issues.title: test_file_utils umask tests assert against a umask the code never reads (import-time _UMASK), so they only pass on a 0o022 host
issues.body:
## Summary

`test_atomic_write_text_new_file_uses_umask_default` and `test_atomic_write_bytes_new_file_uses_umask_default` set a umask at runtime and assert the resulting file mode. `file_utils` captures the umask **once at import**, so the `os.umask(0o022)` the tests call has no effect on the code under test. The assertion therefore only holds on a host whose ambient umask already happens to be `0o022`, and fails outright on any other.

Observed on a host with `umask 0007`:

```
tests/comfy_cli/test_file_utils.py:163: AssertionError
assert 432 == (438 & ~18)
#      ^ 0o660, i.e. 0o666 & ~0o007 (the AMBIENT umask)
#              ^ 0o644, i.e. 0o666 & ~0o022 (the umask the test set)
```

Both tests fail the same way; `test_atomic_write_bytes_…` at `:313`.

## Cause

`comfy_cli/file_utils.py:98-105`:

```python
# The process umask, captured once at import. os has no getter, so reading it
# ...
# overlapping probes can restore each other's zero and strand the umask at 0.
_UMASK = os.umask(0)
os.umask(_UMASK)
```

Capturing once is deliberate and the comment gives a good reason for it. The tests simply do not account for it: they manipulate the real process umask, which `_atomic_write` no longer consults.

So this is a **test** defect, not a product one. The product behaviour the tests mean to pin — "a new destination gets the umask-derived default, not `mkstemp`'s hardcoded 0600" — is correct and worth keeping pinned; the tests just pin it against the wrong knob.

## Suggested fix

Patch the captured value rather than the process umask, so the test controls what the code actually reads:

```python
def test_atomic_write_text_new_file_uses_umask_default(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(file_utils, "_UMASK", 0o022)
    target = tmp_path / "fresh.json"
    atomic_write_text(target, "data")
    assert stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(target).st_mode) == (0o666 & ~0o022)
```

That also removes the `os.umask` save/restore, which is process-global state the current tests mutate.

A second case worth adding while in there: assert the same for a non-`0o022` umask (`0o077`, so `0o600`), which would have caught this — a single hardcoded umask value cannot distinguish "the code honours the umask" from "the host umask matches the literal in the assertion".

## Context

Found while verifying that pre-existing failures were unrelated to a converter change. Two other environment-sensitive failures turned up in the same run and are worth separating:

- Five `tests/comfy_cli/command/test_code_search.py::TestCodeSearchCLI` cases fail when the suite runs from inside an AI coding tool, because `CLAUDECODE` / `AI_AGENT` in the environment flip `detect_caller()` and `code-search` then passes `agent_origin=True`. Fixed in #1072.
- `test_node_deps.py::test_non_pep440_installed_version_is_unknown_not_a_crash` reports `mismatch` where it expects `unknown`. Not agent-env related (it fails with those vars unset) and I have not diagnosed it; noting it so it is not assumed covered by the other two.

None of these fail in CI, which is why they have survived: CI's environment happens to satisfy every one of the assumptions.



### Task Decomposition

Not decomposed: this is a two-test change in one file (swap `os.umask(...)` for `monkeypatch.setattr(file_utils, "_UMASK", ...)`, plus one extra parametrised umask value). Stated explicitly per the issue-filing convention.

issues.title: Jupyter MCP Server’s normalize_filepath() incorrectly handles paths with ‘workspace/’ prefix
issues.body:
##Writed By Human
I redirected the jupyter server log to a document, and catched this.I sent it to AI and it written the following text.I reviewed these contents,and confirmed the Step of Reproduce and ErrorLog,but I'm not very sure about the Analysis.I hope it can be of help.
## Environment
- **Jupyter Server Version:** 2.21.1
- **Jupyter MCP Extension Version:** 3.4.8
- **Python Version:** 3.14.4
- **Operating System:** Linux
- **Jupyter Server Root:** `/home/administrator`
- **Working Directory:** `/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src`

## Summary
When using Jupyter MCP Server tools (specifically `read_notebook`) with file paths containing 'workspace/' as a prefix, the `normalize_filepath()` function incorrectly converts the relative path to an absolute path, dropping the 'workspace/' portion of the path.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start Jupyter Server from `/home/administrator/`
2. Create a file at `/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb`
3. Use the Jupyter MCP Server tool `read_notebook` with the path `'workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb'`
4. Observe the error

## Expected Behavior
The tool should correctly resolve the path to `/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb` and read the file successfully.

## Actual Behavior
The tool fails with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/administrator/development_part_3.ipynb'`

## Error Log
```
[10/17/26 16:20:40] Error calling tool 'read_notebook'                                                                  
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastmcp/server/server.py:1359 in call_tool
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastmcp/tools/base.py:421 in _run
    ... 4 frames hidden ...
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jupyter_ai_tools/toolkits/notebook.py:197 in read_notebook
   194 │   │   The notebook content as a markdown string.
   195 │   """
   196 │   try:
→ 197 │   │   notebook_dict = await read_notebook_json(file_path)
   198 │   │   notebook_md = notebook_json_to_md(notebook_dict, include_outputs=include_outputs)
   199 │   │   return notebook_md
   200 │   except Exception:
  File "/home/administrator/workspace/environments/jupyter/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jupyter_ai_tools/toolkits/notebook.py:242 in read_notebook_json
   239 │   │   return payload["content"]
   240 │
   241 │   normalized_path = normalize_filepath(file_path)
→ 242 │   with open(normalized_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   243 │   │   notebook_dict = json.load(f)
   244 │   │   return notebook_dict
   245
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'/home/administrator/development_part_3.ipynb'
```

## Root Cause Analysis
The `normalize_filepath()` function in `jupyter_ai_tools/toolkits/notebook.py:242` appears to be incorrectly handling paths that contain 'workspace/'. When given a relative path `'workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb'`, it incorrectly normalizes it to `'/home/administrator/development_part_3.ipynb'` instead of the correct `'/home/administrator/workspace/DCSProject/src/development_part_3.ipynb'`.

## Workaround
Currently, the only workaround is to:
1. Either use absolute paths (which may not be supported by all tools)
2. Or adjust the directory structure to avoid the 'workspace/' prefix

## Impact
This bug affects all Jupyter MCP Server tools that rely on file path resolution, particularly in environments where files are organized under directories named 'workspace/', which is a common pattern in development environments and containers.

## Additional Context
- This was discovered while trying to insert a cell into a notebook file using Jupyter MCP tools
- Other paths without the 'workspace/' prefix seem to work correctly
- The bug appears to be in the path normalization logic, not in the basic file reading functionality

issues.title: [BUG] Empty Claude reply fails the run on the direct Anthropic transport (400)
issues.body:
Found while testing LLM provider integrations in agent frameworks: an automated tool flags candidates and each one is reproduced before it is reported. Reproduced on 7e1e5fe (main) against a local fake endpoint, not the live API.

**Describe the bug**
With `PIPESHUB_AGENT_TRANSPORT=direct` and an Anthropic model, a turn where Claude sends back nothing fails the run with a 400 instead of recovering.

The empty reply is stored as an `AssistantMessage`, and `AnthropicTransport` replays it as `{"type": "text", "text": ""}`. Anthropic refuses that with `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty`. The recovery is what sends it: `completion_gate` adds the "Your last reply came through empty" nudge, and the request carrying the nudge also carries the empty block. A thinking-only reply cut off at `max_tokens` fails the same way through the continuation note.

The LangChain arm recovers from the same reply, because langchain-anthropic drops the empty turn.

**To Reproduce**
Real `Agent`, `completion_gate` and the transport `build_direct_transport` picks, with a local endpoint standing in for Anthropic. Its first reply is `{"content": [], "stop_reason": "end_turn"}`, and it answers an empty text block with the error above.

```python
llm = get_generator_model("anthropic", {"configuration": {"apiKey": key, "model": "claude-sonnet-5"},
                                        "isReasoning": True, "isDefault": True})
transport = build_direct_transport(llm, model_name="claude-sonnet-5")
# Agent(spec, runtime) with this transport, streaming on
agent.runtime.hooks.on(HookEvent.POST_MODEL).use(completion_gate(context))
result = await agent.run(Goal(description="What changed this week?"))
```

The second request has roles `user, assistant, user`, with this assistant message:

```text
{"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": ""}]}
```

and the run ends with:

```text
success=False output=None
LLM call failed: Anthropic API error (stream): Error code: 400 - ... 'message': 'messages: text content blocks must be non-empty'
```

The history on its own shows it too: `transport.complete([UserMessage("..."), AssistantMessage(content=""), UserMessage("Please continue.")])`.

**Expected behavior**
The empty turn is left out of the request, the nudge goes out, and the run continues as it does on the LangChain arm.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Version/Commit ID: `2113fd2`
 - `PIPESHUB_AGENT_TRANSPORT=direct`, provider Anthropic, `claude-sonnet-5`

**Related issues**
None found. #4089 reworded the nudge and did not touch this.

**Additional context**
Cause: `_format_message` falls back to an empty text block when an assistant message has no text and no tool calls ([anthropic.py#L287](https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/blob/2113fd22f94f4a5daa25a9e995ae279dc1d17532/backend/python/app/agent_loop_lib/transport/anthropic.py#L287)).

The 400 in the output comes from the local endpoint, which copies the real message. Real reports of that error on this shape: [block/sprout#559](https://github.com/block/sprout/pull/559) (empty `end_turn` reply, same fallback) and [anthropics/claude-code#88536](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/88536) (assistant `{"type":"text","text":""}` replayed to api.anthropic.com). Anthropic documents empty `end_turn` replies and says to "add a continuation prompt in a new user message rather than retrying with the empty response" ([stop reasons](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons)).

Fix idea: skip such a turn in `AnthropicTransport._format_messages`, which leaves `_format_message` and the test pinning its fallback alone. Two user messages in a row are fine, the API merges them, and it is what the LangChain arm already sends.

```python
if isinstance(msg, AssistantMessage) and not msg.tool_calls and not msg.text.strip():
    continue
```

issues.title: [Plugin Request]: Baizhi Agent Toolkit - web search, scraping, and extraction
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

Baizhi Agent Toolkit

### Function Description

Hi Dify team,

I maintain Baizhi Cloud's Agent Toolkit integrations and coordinate product operations. I am submitting this request through `ct-jaryn` on behalf of Baizhi Cloud. We would like to contribute and maintain a native Tool Plugin, and would appreciate feedback on whether the following scope fits the Marketplace's expectations for a distinct integration.

Baizhi Agent Toolkit is a hosted commercial tool service, not an LLM inference provider. Users need their own Baizhi account and API key; tool calls can consume service credits. Our [official integration repository](https://github.com/chaitin/baizhi-agent-toolkit) publishes integration configuration, documentation, and tests, not the hosted backend implementation.

The proposed plugin itself would be free and open source; Baizhi's hosted service usage would be billed separately under its service terms.

#### Proposed user experience

Install the plugin, authorize it with a required provider-level `secret-input` and a link to the [Baizhi console](https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/), then select one of three typed tools in a Workflow or Agent:

- **Web search** (`websearch_search`): search public web sources with query, freshness, result-count, and source-filter parameters.
- **Read a web page** (`web_scrape`): retrieve a page's content from a user-supplied HTTP(S) URL.
- **Extract structured information** (`web_extract`): request specified fields or instruction-driven extraction from a page.

The plugin would use a fixed Streamable HTTP endpoint, `https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/mcp`, with `Authorization: Bearer <user-provided key>`. The credential would not be a model-supplied tool parameter. Public examples, source code, packages, and CI would contain no real key.

#### Difference from existing MCP support

Dify already supports remote MCP and custom headers, and the Marketplace already has general-purpose MCP clients. We are not requesting another generic MCP connector or claiming that native MCP support is missing.

The intended contribution is a service-specific provider credential flow and three stable, typed workflow tools, with maintained parameter/output mapping, bounded errors, documentation, and compatibility tests. The plugin would not accept arbitrary remote tool names or automatically expose newly discovered capabilities. Provider credential validation would use initialization and tool discovery only, not a billable tool invocation. This needs to earn its place as a focused integration rather than merely rebrand a generic client.

#### Safety and review scope

Although the plugin's own MCP connection has a fixed destination, page scraping and extraction delegate user-supplied URL retrieval to the hosted service. We would conservatively disclose **High risk** under the current arbitrary-URL-fetching/crawling criteria, document request timeouts and data flow, and not infer low risk from the fixed transport endpoint. No code execution, shell access, cloud sandbox, payment, or arbitrary-tool forwarding is proposed.

The plugin would need an accurate privacy policy covering the data sent to Baizhi and relevant downstream services, plus credential/logging safeguards. We will not invent data-retention, residency, or no-logging guarantees. The adapter's open-source license and the hosted service's account/usage terms would be disclosed separately.

#### Contribution status and next steps

We have completed a local three-tool prototype from a previously recorded, credential-free tool-schema snapshot. Its 55 offline tests pass with the actual Dify and MCP SDKs and in-memory HTTP transports; a separate local review and rerun also passed. The tests cover provider declarations, typed input mapping, discovery-only credential checks, the fixed endpoint, redirect rejection, bounded discovery, and credential/error/log redaction. These are local results; reviewable source and release artifacts have not yet been published.

The prototype has not been accepted into the Marketplace, validated in a real Dify Community Edition or Cloud workspace, or newly tested against the production service. Historical schemas may have changed. URL validation is not a complete server-side request-forgery defense, and a post-parse output-size check is not a strict transport-memory bound. This issue remains a plugin-scope request, **not a packaged submission or a completed compatibility claim**.

Before a release PR, we would publish reviewable plugin source and setup/troubleshooting documentation, verify current tool schemas and a limited live flow with a dedicated revocable key, complete Dify installation/credential/tool tests, confirm the privacy disclosure and Developer Agreement, and submit one validated `.difypkg` through this repository's current template. Agreement and unperformed-test checkboxes will not be pre-checked.

We would welcome guidance if an existing integration or a different contribution route is more appropriate. Thank you for considering the proposal; the Baizhi team would be glad to cooperate on a maintainable integration that fits Dify's architecture and review standards. This request does not imply Dify endorsement or an established partnership.

### Official Website URL

https://baizhi.cloud/landing/agent-toolkit

issues.title: [Plugin Request]: AnySearch — unified general + vertical AI search
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

AnySearch

### Function Description

**API Docs**

API base: `https://api.anysearch.com` · MCP: `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp`

**Function Description**

AnySearch is a unified search API built for AI agents: one endpoint serving both general web search and vertical, structured data retrieval. We would like to publish it as a community tool plugin in the `search` category (`tags: [search]`, same shape as the official Tavily / Brave providers), and we would rather confirm with the maintainers first that it is welcome alongside the existing search providers — and whether you would prefer a different tag, scope, or risk framing.

**Proposed plugin surface** — three tools, Python 3.12 runner, minimal dependency footprint (`requests` only):

| Tool | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `anysearch_search` | `POST /v1/search` | Unified search. `query` (required), `tag` (`{domain}.{sub_domain}`, e.g. `code.doc`), `params` (object, tag-specific, e.g. `{"ticker":"AAPL"}`), `zone` (`cn` / `intl`), `language`, `max_results` (1–10), `format` (`json` / `markdown`) |
| `anysearch_capabilities` | `GET /v1/sub-domains` | Returns available domains, capability tags and their parameter definitions. Does **not** consume search quota. |
| `anysearch_extract` | `POST /v1/extract` | Fetch and extract clean content (HTML / plain text / JSON / Markdown) from a public URL |

The provider credential would be a `secret-input` API key that is **optional**: unauthenticated calls work against a per-IP rate-limited daily free tier, so users — and reviewers — can evaluate the plugin before signing up. Authenticated calls use `Authorization: Bearer <key>` against a paid quota.

**Why this is not a duplicate of the existing search providers**

The official providers are either general web search (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Serper, SearchApi, SearXNG, Perplexity) or extract/crawl (Jina, Firecrawl). The community vertical ones are single-purpose and region-bound (Google Scholar, Bilibili Search, Webz News Search, Bocha, Baidu AI Search, ZhipuAI Web Search). AnySearch differs on these specific points:

1. **General and vertical from the same endpoint and the same key.** A plain call behaves like general web search; adding `tag=finance.quote` with `params={"type":"crypto"}` returns live market quotes instead of blue links. No second vendor, no second credential, no second plugin.
2. **The vertical catalog is data, not a build-time schema.** `GET /v1/sub-domains` returns the available domains, tags and parameter definitions (`description`, `required`, `sort_order`) at runtime, at no quota cost. The plugin surface therefore stays at three tools as the catalog grows, instead of needing a new tool or plugin release per vertical.
3. **Intent routing and result fusion.** Per our docs, `/v1/search` routes the query to the best underlying sources by intent and then fuses and re-ranks the results — the caller does not pick an engine or merge result sets by hand.
4. **Region routing.** `zone: cn | intl` selects the result universe inside one API, instead of needing separate CN and global plugins.
5. **No-key first run.** Verified: an anonymous `POST /v1/search` returns `code: 0` with results, so a user can try the tool before creating an account.
6. **Low integration cost.** An MCP server is already live over Streamable HTTP at `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp` (anonymous or Bearer), and a Skill package already exists — the native tool plugin can be built and reviewed against a working endpoint rather than a spec.

**Questions for the maintainers** — we would rather ask before opening the PR:

1. **Category / overlap.** We could not find a published policy on category overlap (`CONTRIBUTING.md` is still `TODO`). Is another `search`-tagged provider welcome, or would you prefer it under a distinct tag or label to keep the category legible?
2. **Optional credentials.** Is an optional API key acceptable for a search-category provider, given that most existing providers require one? If not, we will make the key required and drop the anonymous path in the plugin.
3. **Risk classification.** `POST /v1/extract` fetches user-supplied URLs. Reading `docs/plugin-submission-requirements.md`, we believe that places the plugin at High risk ("proxy or crawl arbitrary URLs"). We intend to declare High and constrain inputs, set request timeouts, and avoid leaking credentials in errors. Please confirm that is the level you expect, and whether a High-risk plugin in the search category is acceptable.
4. **Exposed tag set.** The live catalog is broader than what a typical Dify user needs, and includes health, financial and legal data alongside some legally sensitive sources. We are happy to restrict the tag set the plugin exposes. Would you like us to, and do you have guidance on which verticals a search provider in the Marketplace should surface?
5. **Listing path.** We assume the expected route is a PR to `langgenius/dify-plugins` adding `anysearch/anysearch/anysearch-<version>.difypkg`, with `PRIVACY.md`, a source-repository link and an English README. If you would instead prefer to handle AnySearch as an official / featured integration, or an MCP-only listing, tell us and we will follow that path.

We are happy to adjust scope to whatever keeps the Marketplace coherent. Thanks.

### Official Website URL

https://anysearch.com/docs

issues.title: Kubernetes sandbox backend (no Docker socket)
issues.body:
## Problem

Every sandbox starts a sibling container through the `docker` CLI and
`/var/run/docker.sock`. That covers Agent Python tools and skills, the Code
node and its formatter, custom Playwright, MCP stdio, and the Codex and
OpenCode wrappers.

Some Kubernetes nodes have no Docker daemon: Talos, Bottlerocket,
containerd-only pools on EKS, AKS and GKE, and OpenShift. There, the only
choice is `HEYM_*_SANDBOX=subprocess`, which the docs call trusted
single-user only, or nothing. The Code node, Codex and OpenCode have no
fallback and fail.

## Who hits it

Anyone self-hosting Heym on Kubernetes, where mounting the host's Docker
socket is either impossible or not something you would want to do.

## Proposed approach

Three PRs, each releasable on its own:

1. **No behaviour change.** Move the nine `docker run` builders behind one
   `SandboxSpec` plus a `DockerRunner`. Parity tests assert that the argv
   stays the same, flag for flag. This also removes the five copies of
   `_docker_available`, `_resolve_image` and `_force_remove_container`.
2. **`HEYM_SANDBOX_BACKEND=kubernetes`, for the stdin/stdout-only sites:**
   the Python tool, the Code formatter, the Code node without requirements,
   and Playwright.
    - Each run is one Pod in a configurable namespace, under Pod Security
      `restricted`, with no ServiceAccount token.
    - `--network none|bridge` becomes a pod label that operator-provided
      NetworkPolicies select.
    - It is built on `httpx` and `websockets`, so there is no new dependency.
    - It fails closed exactly as the Docker path does.
3. **Workspaces.** Skills, Code node requirements and MCP stdio first, then
   Codex and OpenCode. There are two modes, and each run sees only its own
   files in both:
    - `stream` (default): a tar over the pod's attach stream, the same way
      `kubectl cp` moves files. No storage needed.
    - `volume`: an RWX PVC mounted with `subPath` set to the run's directory,
      the Kubernetes equivalent of today's `volume-subpath`.

Docker stays the default. No schema, migration, UI or public API changes.

## Touches

- `backend/app/services/*_executor.py`
- `mcp_stdio_sandbox.py`
- `playwright_sandbox.py`
- `code_formatter.py`
- `docker/heym-*-docker`
- `ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md`

## Questions

1. Do you want a Kubernetes backend in-tree, or would you rather Docker stay
   the only supported sandbox?
2. Is the `SandboxSpec` plus runner shape right for PR 1? I'd rather agree on
   it here than in a large diff.
3. Codex's bubblewrap cannot run in a `restricted` pod. Is
   `--sandbox danger-full-access` acceptable when the pod is the boundary?
4. Would a Helm chart help, either in-tree under `deploy/helm/` or as a
   separate community chart on Artifact Hub? It would package Heym plus the
   sandbox namespace, RBAC and NetworkPolicies, with presets for OpenShift,
   EKS, AKS and GKE. I'd maintain it, including tag bumps.

I have a prototype that matches the current argv of all nine call sites and
am happy to share it. I'll wait for your go-ahead on scope, and can talk it
through on Discord first if that's easier.

issues.title: Flagship eval did not pass on v0.25.4-rc1
issues.body:
The flagship eval on release tag `v0.25.4-rc1` did not pass. Publishing is not blocked by it.

- Run: https://github.com/amd/gaia/actions/runs/41148504198
- Tier: `smoke` (eval/ci_tiers.json)
- Scenario lanes: `failure`
- Outcomes (`gaia eval tasks`): `skipped`
- Final tag, full sweep found for this commit or an RC: `skipped` (`skipped` on an RC)

Start with the run's summary page: it names which lanes measured, which measured nothing, and
how long each took. Then download the failing lane's `eval-<lane>` artifact - it carries the
transcripts, judge rationales, backend log and Lemonade logs. Those machines are ephemeral and
already destroyed, so the artifact is the only copy, and it expires in 14 days.

Compare with the previous tag's run first. A failure no change since then explains usually means
the environment moved, not the code: a Lemonade version bump, a re-quantised model, a driver or
runner-image change.

`cancelled` rather than `failure` means no measurement happened at all - a manual cancel, or a
lane that waited out GitHub's 24h queue limit. Re-dispatch the workflow on the tag.

A passing re-run closes this issue, and so does a later passing tag on the same major.minor line
whose tier covers this one (a full sweep covers smoke). A final tag's issue closes only on its own
passing re-run.

issues.title: IPv6 address still in duplicate address detection is skipped and never retried
issues.body:
## Problem

A link-local IPv6 address that is still in duplicate address detection (DAD, "tentative") cannot be bound. `new_socket` treats `EADDRNOTAVAIL` as benign, logs a warning and returns `None`, so the interface gets no responder socket. `add_interface` then drops the multicast group membership it had just joined for that interface.

Nothing retries the bind. Once DAD finishes (about a second later) the address is usable, but the address set has not changed, so a caller that reconciles on address changes has no reason to call `async_update_interfaces` again. The instance stays without IPv6 on that interface until some unrelated address change.

## Where

- [`new_socket`](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_utils/net.py#L268-L274) returns `None` on `EADDRNOTAVAIL`.
- [`add_interface`](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_utils/net.py#L462-L480) drops the group membership when the responder socket could not be created.

This affects both construction (`create_sockets`) and `async_update_interfaces`.

## Reproduce

Start a container on an IPv6-enabled Docker network and construct `AsyncZeroconf(ip_version=IPVersion.All)` as soon as the process starts:

```
docker network create --ipv6 --subnet fd00:dead:beef::/64 zc6test
docker run --rm --network zc6test <image> python -c "..."
```

Log output:

```
WARNING zeroconf: Address not available when binding to ('fe80::943f:67ff:fe01:cbb8', 5353, 0, 11), it is expected to happen on some systems
```

The instance has an IPv4 sender only. Calling `async_update_interfaces()` a few seconds later binds the link-local sender.

Seen with 0.151.2 on Linux (arm64, Python 3.13). The same window exists whenever an interface comes up shortly before construction or a reconcile, for example at container or host boot.

## Suggested fix

Treat `EADDRNOTAVAIL` on an IPv6 address as retryable: remember the interfaces skipped for that reason and schedule one short internal retry (a few seconds), for both construction and `async_update_interfaces`.

Filtering tentative addresses up front is not an option, since `ifaddr` does not expose `IFA_F_TENTATIVE`.

## Workaround

esphome/device-builder#2864 runs one extra `async_update_interfaces` ten seconds after startup and after each binding change.

issues.title: feat(computer): prompt-bound answer identity for avibe.confirm (quick-reply buttons per surface)
issues.body:
**Scope (re-scoped per source decision on #2645):** this issue now tracks only **option B, a prompt-bound answer identity for `avibe.confirm()`**.

Items 1–3 below were fixed directly in #2645 and are kept here only for history:

1. The route cap is now sized for the worst-case JSON envelope.
2. Unattended (scheduled) Turns are refused with `confirm_unattended` before any prompt is sent.
3. Only direct original text replies can answer a confirm; quick replies (`quick_reply_for`), forwards, and edits are ordinary messages.

## Option B: prompt-bound answer identity

Today a confirm answer is a plain-text yes/no that names no prompt. #2645 limits a Session to one pending confirm and matches only direct original replies, so the remaining ambiguity is an unrelated standalone "yes" from the approver while a confirm is pending. That reply is still taken as the answer.

Goal: render each confirm with yes/no quick-reply buttons on every surface, and accept only an answer bound to that exact prompt.

- Web: the reply's `quick_reply_for` must equal the confirm prompt's message id.
- Each IM surface: the button callback must carry the prompt's identity.

Free-text yes/no would then no longer resolve a confirm, or would only do so under an explicit, documented fallback. Handle this in a separate PR. It touches per-platform button callbacks, so it needs its own design and tests.

Origin: https://github.com/avibe-bot/avibe/pull/2645 (review threads r4291828071, r4291828083, r4291828085).

issues.title: Computer Use: confirm deadline and driver idle TTL follow-ups from #2838
issues.body:
Follow-up from #2838 (Computer Use driver session idle expiry). Report-only findings; nothing here blocks #2838.

## 1. A human confirm is bounded by the generic 300 s script deadline (P2)

- `vibe computer run` has no `--timeout`; every run uses `DEFAULT_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300` (`vibe/computer_script_runner.py`). `avibe.confirm(...)` has no bound of its own, so a confirm waiting on a person gets whatever is left of that 300 s.
- The Controller already admits script connections up to 3600 s (`core/computer_script_sessions.py`, `_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`).
- Live acceptance case: the owner did not see the prompt in time, and the script ended with `script_timeout` at step `avibe.confirm` (`ambiguous: true`).

Options: give confirm its own longer bound, or expose `--timeout` on `vibe computer run` up to the Controller ceiling.

## 2. A wait of more than 5 minutes retires the script's element tokens (P2, design together with 1)

- cua-driver 0.31.0 retires a named session after `DEFAULT_SESSION_IDLE_TTL = 5 min`. #2838 makes the Controller start the session again on the driver's pre-dispatch "session has ended" refusal, so Computer Use no longer dies for the Avibe Session.
- The driver still retires the earlier episode's element tokens and snapshots. A script that resumes after a confirm wait of more than 5 minutes therefore gets `observe_first` on its next input, so the SDK has to `waitFor` or observe again.
- A longer confirm bound alone would make this case common. Decide whether the SDK re-acquires its handles after a long `confirm`, whether the Controller keeps the driver session warm while a confirm is pending, or whether the confirm bound stays under the driver TTL.

issues.title: computer-use: launch() cannot reopen a running app's hidden main window
issues.body:
## Summary

When an app is running but its main window has been closed to the background, minimized, or the app is hidden (⌘H), Computer Use cannot bring the window back. `app.launch()` returns the pid but no window appears. `win.activate()` (`bring_to_front`) brings the process to the front without showing the window, and reports `bring_to_front_exact_window_unverified` (`process_activated=true, focused=false`). The owner has to click the Dock icon before any Agent can continue.

## Evidence (3.2.4rc1, owner machine, 2026-10-30)

Target: an Electron chat app (QQ) whose main window was put into each state below. Setup used only the window's own close and minimize buttons and app hide.

| Window state | Driver `launch_app` today | LaunchServices reopen without activation (`open -g -b <bundle_id>`) | Frontmost app afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| Closed to background | no on-screen window after 6 s | on screen in about 1.3 s | unchanged (Avibe) |
| Minimized | — | restored in about 1.3 s | unchanged |
| App hidden (⌘H) | — | restored in about 1.3 s | unchanged |
| On another Space | untested | untested | — |

## Root cause

At pinned `cua-driver-rs-v0.31.0` (`5272e492`), `launch_app` → `apps::launch_app` → `nsworkspace::open_application` sets `activates = false` and always attaches a synthetic `aevt/oapp` AppleEvent (`apps/nsworkspace.rs`). An app that is already running ignores `oapp`. A Dock click, or `open` on a running app, sends `aevt/rapp` (`kAEReopenApplication`) instead, and that event makes the app show its main window. Upstream `main` still has the same code path.

## Proposed fix

Patch the pinned driver: when the target app is already running, `launch_app` sends `kAEReopenApplication` instead of `oapp`. Keep `activates = false` and the existing focus-steal suppression, so the window comes back without taking the foreground.

- Tool name, schema, and description stay unchanged. The committed tool snapshot records the patch SHA-256, however, so its digest still moves. Follow the #3062 compatibility pattern: a newer Runtime also accepts the previous snapshot digest.
- Update `desktop/cua-driver/PATCHES.md`, `sources.json`, and `prepare-cua-driver.py` provenance.
- Add a deterministic AppKit fixture for the GUI acceptance: it hides its window on close and shows it again on reopen.
- Update the Computer Use Skill: when no on-screen window matches, call `app.launch()` once, then `app.waitFor({ onScreen: true })`. If no window appears, stop and ask the owner, as today. Never loop.
- Open the same fix upstream as a PR to trycua/cua, and add it to the patch's `upstream_refs` and upgrade plan.

## Acceptance

- Each of the three states above returns to the screen through `app.launch()`, and the previously frontmost app stays in front.
- First launch of a not-running app is unchanged.
- The driver tool snapshot is unchanged, or covered by compatibility tests.
- Live GUI check on the owner machine with a packaged build.

## Out of scope

- Foreground clicks that are ignored when the target window is not yet active: separate follow-up.
- Driver `unverifiable` click effects: by design, covered by the Skill since #3074.

issues.title: rewire router on chat reconnect when a room is cleaned up and recreated
issues.body:
Title: fix: rewire router on chat reconnect when a room is cleaned up and recreated

Body:


## Problem

`connect_chat` treats "chat_id already in `active_chats`" as a no-op:

    if chat_id in self.active_chats:
        self.log.warning(f"Chat {chat_id} already connected to router")
        return

When a collaboration room is torn down and recreated — e.g. the client's
WebSocket drops (browser tab closed, laptop sleeps) and the room is freed
after the document cleanup delay, then the user reopens the chat — the router
is *not* told the room went away (there is no stop/reset event when
`jupyter-server-documents` is not installed), so `active_chats[chat_id]` still
holds the old, stopped chat.

On reconnect, `connect_chat(chat_id, new_chat)` hits the stale guard and
returns early. Two consequences:

1. `message_observers[chat_id]` stays bound to the *old* chat's message stream,
   so messages typed in the recreated room are never routed (submitting a
   message does nothing).
2. `_notify_chat_init_observers` never fires, so the persona manager is never
   re-created and the bottom persona picker does not appear.

## Fix

Detect the reconnect case — same `chat_id` but a *different* chat object — and
rewire instead of bailing out: detach the old chat and notify stop observers,
then fall through to the normal connect path with the new chat.

    if chat_id in self.active_chats:
        if self.active_chats[chat_id] is chat:
            self.log.warning(f"Chat {chat_id} already connected to router")
            return
        self.log.warning(f"Chat {chat_id} reconnected with a new chat; rewiring router")
        self.disconnect_chat(chat_id)
        self._notify_chat_stop_observers(chat_id)

    self.active_chats[chat_id] = chat
Suggested commit message:


fix: rewire router when a chat reconnects after room cleanup

connect_chat bailed out whenever chat_id was already in active_chats.
After a room is freed and recreated (client disconnect + cleanup delay,
no stop event without jupyter-server-documents), the stale entry made
the router skip rewiring: new messages went unrouted and no persona
manager was recreated. Detect same-id/different-object and rewire.

issues.title: fix: stop the exact persona manager instance on chat stop (avoid killing a recreated manager)
issues.body:
## Problem

`_on_router_chat_stop` schedules the shutdown by ID only:

    task = self.event_loop.create_task(self._stop_persona_manager(chat_id))

and `_stop_persona_manager` re-fetches the manager by ID when the async task
finally runs:

    persona_manager = persona_managers.get(chat_id)
    ...
    finally:
        persona_managers.pop(chat_id, None)

If the chat reconnects in the meantime, `_on_router_chat_init` installs a fresh
`PersonaManager` for the same `chat_id` *before* the queued stop task runs. The
stop task then looks up by ID, shuts down the *new* manager, and unconditionally
pops the entry — tearing down the manager that just reconnected (persona picker
gone, messages unrouted).

## Fix

Capture the instance to stop synchronously in `_on_router_chat_stop` and pass it
through; `_stop_persona_manager` shuts down the captured instance and only
removes the settings entry if it still points at that same instance.

    def _on_router_chat_stop(self, chat_id: str) -> None:
        ...
        persona_manager = persona_managers.get(chat_id)
        if persona_manager is None:
            return
        task = self.event_loop.create_task(
            self._stop_persona_manager(chat_id, persona_manager)
        )
        self._stopping_chats[chat_id] = task

    async def _stop_persona_manager(
        self, chat_id: str, persona_manager: PersonaManager | None = None
    ) -> None:
        async with self._stop_lock:
            persona_managers = self.serverapp.web_app.settings['jupyter-ai']['persona-managers']
            if persona_manager is None:
                persona_manager = persona_managers.get(chat_id)
            if persona_manager is None:
                return
            try:
                await persona_manager.shutdown_personas()
                ...
            finally:
                if persona_managers.get(chat_id) is persona_manager:
                    persona_managers.pop(chat_id, None)
                self._stopping_chats.pop(chat_id, None)
Suggested commit message:


fix: stop the captured persona manager instance on chat stop

_on_router_chat_stop scheduled _stop_persona_manager(chat_id), which
re-fetched by ID when the async task ran; a reconnect installing a new
manager in between got shut down and popped instead. Capture the instance
up front and only pop the settings entry if it still matches.

issues.title: [BUG] Multiple estimators mutate NumPy's global RNG state
issues.body:
## Description

The conformance test `test_scenario_does_not_modify_global_numpy_rng`, introduced in [[PR #11395](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11395)](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11395), identifies multiple estimators whose test scenarios modify NumPy's process-global random number generator (RNG) state.

The test checks whether an estimator scenario changes the global NumPy RNG state between the beginning and end of execution. A change in this state indicates that the estimator or one of its dependencies may be using NumPy's global RNG instead of an isolated random state.

## Affected estimators

The following 17 estimators have been confirmed to fail this conformance test:

1. `TSCGridSearchCV`
2. `TimeSeriesSVC`
3. `STLBootstrapTransformer`
4. `DirectTabularRegressionForecaster`
5. `VARReduce`
6. `Catch22Classifier`
7. `TrendForecaster`
8. `YfromX`
9. `PolynomialTrendForecaster`
10. `SupervisedTimeSeriesForest`
11. `TimeSeriesForestRegressor`
12. `RandomIntervalClassifier`
13. `ShapeDTW`
14. `IndividualTDE`
15. `KNeighborsTimeSeriesRegressor`
16. `TEASER`
17. `ContractableBOSS`

The original test run identified 33 failing parametrized scenarios associated with these estimators.

The affected scenarios include:

- `ClassifierFitPredict`
- `ClassifierFitPredictThreeClasses`
- `ClassifierFitPredictMultivariate`
- `ClassifierFitPredictUnequalLength`
- `ForecasterFitPredictMultivariateNoX`
- `ForecasterFitPredictUnivariateWithX`

Not every estimator fails every scenario.

```

Before the targeted skips were introduced, the test run reported:

```text
41 failed, 776 passed, 1848 warnings
```

Of the 41 failures:

- **33 failures** were confirmed global NumPy RNG state violations involving the estimators listed above.
- **8 failures** were unrelated `RocketRegressor` API failures. The affected scenarios attempted to call `predict_proba`, which `RocketRegressor` does not expose, resulting in:

```text
AttributeError: 'RocketRegressor' object has no attribute 'predict_proba'
```

These eight failures are not classified as RNG violations.

## Temporary handling in [PR #11395](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11395)

Following the review feedback on [PR #11395](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11395), the 17 confirmed estimators have been added to the existing `tests:skip_by_name` mechanism for the specific conformance test:

`test_scenario_does_not_modify_global_numpy_rng`

This is a targeted exclusion only. The estimators are **not being skipped from testing generally**, and their other applicable tests remain enabled.

No estimator implementation changes or root-cause fixes are included in this temporary handling.

## Expected follow-up

The underlying RNG behavior should be investigated for each affected estimator.

Where applicable, estimators should use isolated random state handling rather than modifying NumPy's process-global RNG state. The conformance test should be re-enabled for each estimator once the corresponding issue has been addressed.

## Verification after temporary skips

After adding the targeted skips, the conformance test selection reported:

```text
8 failed, 769 passed, 1604 warnings
```

The remaining eight failures were the unrelated `RocketRegressor` `predict_proba` API failures. No confirmed global NumPy RNG assertion failures remained among the executed scenarios.

## References

- [[PR #11395 – Test that estimators do not mutate global NumPy RNG](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11395)](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11395)
- [[sktime repository](https://github.com/sktime/sktime)](https://github.com/sktime/sktime)
- Test: `TestAllEstimators.test_scenario_does_not_modify_global_numpy_rng`

issues.title: PERF: pd.eval() copies the whole result in reconstruct_object
issues.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this issue exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this issue exists on the main branch of pandas.


### Reproducible Example


```python
import timeit

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
df1, df2, df3, df4 = (pd.DataFrame(rng.random((20_000, 100))) for _ in range(4))
g = globals()

# fused numexpr kernel, then the result is rebuilt with a full copy
t_eval = min(timeit.repeat("pd.eval('df1 + df2 + df3 + df4')", globals=g, number=5, repeat=5)) / 5

# same computation without the result copy: evaluate ndarrays, re-attach the axes
expr = repr("df1.values + df2.values + df3.values + df4.values")
stmt = f"pd.DataFrame(pd.eval({expr}), index=df1.index, columns=df1.columns, copy=False)"
t_nocopy = min(timeit.repeat(stmt, globals=g, number=5, repeat=5)) / 5

print(f"pd.eval():                        {t_eval * 1e3:6.1f} ms")
print(f"eval on .values + DataFrame(...): {t_nocopy * 1e3:6.1f} ms")
```

Example output from one run (min of 5×5 `timeit` repetitions; 12-round medians for the two statements are 10.6 ms and 4.0 ms):

```
pd.eval():                         11.0 ms
eval on .values + DataFrame(...):   5.0 ms
```

Roughly half of the call is spent copying a result that pandas just allocated. (The `.values` variant is only a way to measure that copy — it skips index alignment, so it is not a suggested API. The 20,000 × 100 size was chosen so that the chained-operator baseline still uses numexpr: the gate is `left_op.size > _MIN_ELEMENTS` (`_MIN_ELEMENTS = 1_000_000`, `pandas/core/computation/expressions.py:47`, gate at `:101`); below it the operator path silently falls back to numpy and the comparison stops being apples-to-apples.)

`cProfile` on the 100,000 × 100 case confirms the call tree (recreate the frames at that size first; trimmed; absolute times under cProfile are inflated, so read the tree, not the split):

```python
import cProfile
cProfile.run("pd.eval('df1 + df2 + df3 + df4')", sort="cumulative")
```

```
   ncalls  tottime  percall  cumtime  percall filename:lineno(function)
        1    0.006    0.006    0.030    0.030 .../computation/eval.py:200(eval)
        1    0.000    0.000    0.022    0.022 .../computation/engines.py:68(evaluate)
        1    0.000    0.000    0.012    0.012 .../computation/align.py:180(reconstruct_object)
        1    0.000    0.000    0.012    0.012 .../core/frame.py:466(__init__)
        1    0.000    0.000    0.012    0.012 .../internals/construction.py:196(ndarray_to_mgr)
        1    0.012    0.012    0.012    0.012 {built-in method numpy.array}
        1    0.000    0.000    0.009    0.009 .../computation/engines.py:115(_evaluate)
        1    0.000    0.000    0.009    0.009 .../necompiler.py:935(evaluate)
        1    0.009    0.009    0.009    0.009 .../necompiler.py:1045(re_evaluate)
```

(`numpy.array` is a leaf: no child events, the time is the copy itself.)

A larger version (100,000 × 100 × 4), medians of 12 interleaved rounds, two independent runs:

| variant | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `df1 + df2 + df3 + df4` | 29.1 ms | 29.3 ms |
| `pd.eval("df1 + df2 + df3 + df4")` | 28.8 ms | 27.1 ms |
| `pd.eval(...)` with `copy=False` for the owned numexpr result (prototype) | **10.4 ms** | **10.4 ms** |
| `pd.eval` on `.values`, then `DataFrame(..., copy=False)` | 10.0 ms | 10.0 ms |

The median per-round paired difference `pd.eval - pd.eval(copy=False)` was 18.3 ms (run 1) and 16.4 ms (run 2); individual rounds are bimodal (14–31 ms), see the timing note below.
